summary: Scholze defines perfectoid fields, perfectoid K-algebras and perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid field K and proves the tilting equivalences: perfectoid K-algebras ≅ perfectoid K♭-algebras through their almost-integral structures (Theorem 5.2), Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) identifying rational subsets, with perfectoid rational localisations, the sheaf property and almost vanishing of H^i(X, 𝒪⁺) (Theorem 6.3), perfectoid spaces over K ≅ over K♭ (Proposition 6.17), a strong almost purity theorem (Theorem 7.9) and an isomorphism of étale sites X_ét ≅ X♭_ét (Theorem 7.12). For toric varieties he identifies |X^ad_{Σ,K♭}| and its étale topos with the inverse limit along the p-power map (Theorem 8.5), approximates complete intersections by tilted subvarieties (Corollary 8.8), and deduces Deligne's weight-monodromy conjecture for set-theoretic complete intersections in projective smooth toric varieties over p-adic fields (Theorem 9.6). The atlas already follows §§3–7 closely: the reviewed PerfectoidSpaces decomposition is a node-by-node extraction of this paper, so those 90-odd items are planned by P0–P3, P5 and P7; §2's recall of Huber's theory is largely in Tau Ceti or planned by its roadmap Foundations of adic spaces. What the atlas lacks: Huber's comparison of rigid-analytic varieties, formal models and taut spaces with adic spaces and the field-pair description of points (source routes to AdicSpacesPartII and TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic); three small statements for P1 and P3; the toric geometry of §8 over nonarchimedean fields with its perfectoid tower and approximation (a continuation of Analytic toric geometry beside its existing Part II, ShimuraCompactifications, whose toric charts it imports; it also supplies the construction leaves that the toric proposal of PAPER-BINDA-KATO-VEZZANI-25, now under revision, lacked); the ℓ-adic weight-monodromy theorem of §9, a continuation of Deligne weights, purity and the Weil bounds beside its existing Part II, WeightsInEtaleCohomology; and the weight–monodromy predicate for a Weil–Deligne representation, a source route to DWP.5.

items.name: Fontaine–Wintenberger: Gal(ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞})) ≅ Gal(𝔽_p((t)))
items.statement: The absolute Galois groups of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) and of 𝔽_p((t)) are canonically isomorphic. Proof outline in the paper: with K the completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) and K♭ the completion of 𝔽_p((t))(t^{1/p^∞}), one has K°/p = ℤ_p[p^{1/p^∞}]/p ≅ 𝔽_p[t^{1/p^∞}]/t = K♭°/t (p^{1/p^n} ↦ t^{1/p^n}), a continuous multiplicative non-additive map x ↦ x♯ from K♭ to K sending t to p, and K♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} K; for a finite extension L of K♭ that is the splitting field of a separable monic polynomial, L♯ is the splitting field of the polynomial whose coefficients are the ♯ of the p^n-th roots of the original ones, for n large; these fields stabilise.
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.1 and the paragraph after it, pp. 245–246
items.note: A special case of Theorem 1.3 (item 3, from item 42). The step from the algebraic fields to their completions uses that a henselian valued field and its completion have the same absolute Galois group, and that the purely inseparable extension 𝔽_p((t)) ⊂ 𝔽_p((t))(t^{1/p^∞}) does not change it; the paper does not say so (source issue E5, already recorded in the atlas as PerfectoidSpaces/E23). That comparison is item 2, routed with P3. The decomposition node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields plans Theorem 3.7.

items.name: Absolute Galois groups are unchanged by completion and by perfection
items.statement: For a henselian nonarchimedean valued field F with completion F̂, restriction G_{F̂} → G_F is an isomorphism (Krasner's lemma); and a purely inseparable extension does not change the absolute Galois group. Used for ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}) and 𝔽_p((t))(t^{1/p^∞}) in Theorem 1.1, and for k(ϖ^{1/p^∞}) and 𝔽_q((t)) in the proof of Theorem 9.6.
items.locator: §1, the paragraph after Theorem 1.1, pp. 245–246; §9, proof of Theorem 9.6, p. 309
items.note: Planned by P3 in the PerfectoidSpaces blueprint packet (research/blueprint/packets/PerfectoidSpaces--P0.json, 324 nodes over P0–P7): its node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger states the application to Theorem 1.1 with both invariances, the completion step from P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (b) and the purely inseparable step from P3/finite-etale-under-completed-perfection. Mathlib has Krasner's lemma (IsKrasner) and Field.absoluteGaloisGroup, not the comparison. The paper uses the reduction without comment, which is standard and not a source mistake (E5, rejected on review).

items.name: Absolute Galois groups of a perfectoid field and its tilt
items.statement: For every perfectoid field K with tilt K♭, the absolute Galois groups of K and K♭ are canonically isomorphic (via the degree-preserving equivalence L ↦ L♭ between finite extensions of K and of K♭).
items.locator: §1, Theorem 1.3, p. 246; deduced from Theorem 3.7, p. 267
items.note: Planned by P3 through Theorem 3.7 (node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields). The Galois-group form is the corollary of the equivalence of finite étale sites of Spec K and Spec K♭ (both are Galois categories); Mathlib has the Galois-category and Galois-correspondence machinery (CategoryTheory.PreGaloisCategory, IsGalois.intermediateFieldEquivSubgroup).

items.name: The tilted affine line as an inverse limit (Claim 1.4, Theorem 1.5)
items.statement: Claim 1.4 (heuristic): the affine line over K♭ "is" lim_{T↦T^p} of the affine line over K. Theorem 1.5: there is a homeomorphism of topological spaces |(𝔸¹_{K♭})^ad| ≅ lim_{T↦T^p} |(𝔸¹_K)^ad|, where K is a perfectoid field with tilt K♭; on points it is given by x ↦ (x♯, (x^{1/p})♯, …).
items.note: The body proves the analogous statement for the adic toric space of a fan (Theorem 8.5(iii)). For the complete fan of ℙ¹, X^ad_Σ is (ℙ¹)^ad, and the Frobenius φ(x_0 : x_1) = (x_0^p : x_1^p) preserves ∞ and its complement, so restricting the homeomorphism to 𝔸¹ = ℙ¹ ∖ {∞} gives Theorem 1.5; the extraction's source issue E9 was rejected on review for this reason. Routed with the toric Part II, which states Theorem 1.5 as this restriction.

items.name: Faltings's almost purity theorem in the smooth case, recovered
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field of characteristic 0, R_n = K°⟨T_1^{±1/p^n}, …, T_d^{±1/p^n}⟩, R_∞ = lim R_n, R̂_∞ its p-adic completion and R = R̂_∞[1/p] (a perfectoid K-algebra). If S_n is a finite normal R_n-algebra that is étale after inverting p, S_m (m ≥ n) the integral closure of R_m in (S_n ⊗_{R_n} R_m)[1/p] and S_∞ = lim S_m, then with S = S_n ⊗_{R_n} R (finite étale over R) one has S° = Ŝ_∞, S° is almost finite étale over R° = R̂_∞ (Theorem 7.9(iii)), and S_∞ is almost finite étale over R_∞ — which is Faltings's almost purity theorem [Faltings 1988, Theorem 3.1].
items.note: Planned by P3 in the PerfectoidSpaces blueprint packet (research/blueprint/packets/PerfectoidSpaces--P0.json, 324 nodes over P0–P7): an acceptance criterion of PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem is that Faltings's original almost purity (toric charts over a discretely valued field) is recovered by base change to the perfectoid tower (Kedlaya–Liu Remark 5.5.10). The paper only sketches this: the identification S° = Ŝ_∞ and the descent from the completed to the uncompleted tower are asserted, so the P3 blueprint must write them out; Sch12 is a source for it.

items.name: Nonarchimedean field
items.statement: A nonarchimedean field is a topological field k whose topology is induced by a nontrivial valuation of rank 1. It admits a norm |·| : k → ℝ_{≥0}, unique up to the automorphisms x ↦ x^α (0 < α < ∞) of ℝ_{≥0}. In §2 k is fixed and assumed complete.
items.locator: §2, Definition 2.1 and the sentences after it, p. 252
items.note: Mathlib expresses a nonarchimedean field as a nontrivially normed field with an ultrametric distance, or as a valued field with a rank-one valuation (Valuation.RankOne); equivalent absolute values differ by a real power (AbsoluteValue.isEquiv_iff_exists_rpow_eq, Mathlib/Analysis/AbsoluteValue/Equivalence.lean:331).

items.name: Valuations and continuous valuations
items.statement: A valuation on a ring R is a multiplicative map |·| : R → Γ ∪ {0}, Γ a totally ordered abelian group written multiplicatively, with |0| = 0, |1| = 1 and |x + y| ≤ max(|x|, |y|). If R is a topological ring, |·| is continuous if {x ∈ R : |x| < γ} is open for every γ ∈ Γ. (Remark 2.3: for Γ = ℝ_{>0} this is a seminorm; Huber's terminology is kept.)
items.note: Mathlib's Valuation (Mathlib/RingTheory/Valuation/Basic.lean:80). Tau Ceti's Valuation.IsContinuous (TauCeti/RingTheory/Valuation/Continuous/Basic.lean:123) quantifies over attained values v(b) rather than all of Γ; its docstring notes the two agree when right multiplication is continuous (isOpen_lt_div), which holds for topological rings.

items.name: Valuation rings, support and the factorisation through the residue field
items.statement: A valuation ring is an integral domain R such that for every nonzero x in its fraction field K, x or x^{-1} lies in R. A valuation |·| on a field K gives the valuation subring {x : |x| ≤ 1}; conversely a valuation ring R ⊂ K gives a valuation with values in K^×/R^× (x ≤ y iff x = yz with z ∈ R), and up to equivalence this is a bijection between valuation subrings of K and valuations on K. For a valuation |·| on a ring R, Γ_{|·|} is the subgroup generated by the nonzero values, supp(|·|) = {x : |x| = 0} is a prime ideal, and |·| factors as R → K = Frac(R/supp) → Γ ∪ {0}, with valuation ring R(|·|) = {x ∈ K : |x| ≤ 1}.
items.note: All in Mathlib (ValuationSubring.lean:170, 440, 459; Valuation/Basic.lean:1026; Valuation/Quotient.lean:38).

items.name: Equivalence of valuations
items.statement: Two valuations |·|, |·|′ on R are equivalent if the following equivalent conditions hold: (i) there is an isomorphism of totally ordered groups α : Γ_{|·|} ≅ Γ_{|·|′} with |·|′ = α ∘ |·|; (ii) supp(|·|) = supp(|·|′) and R(|·|) = R(|·|′); (iii) for all a, b ∈ R, |a| ≥ |b| if and only if |a|′ ≥ |b|′.
items.note: Mathlib's Valuation.IsEquiv is form (iii). Tau Ceti represents a point of Spv A as a valuative relation (TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/ValuationSpectrum.lean:73), i.e. an equivalence class in the sense of (iii). The comparison with forms (i) and (ii) for rings (not only fields) is not stated as one theorem; for fields, Valuation.isEquiv_iff_val_le_one gives (ii) ⇔ (iii).

items.name: Tate k-algebras, bounded and power-bounded elements, affinoid k-algebras, topologically finite type
items.statement: (i) A Tate k-algebra is a topological k-algebra R with a subring R₀ such that aR₀ (a ∈ k^×) is a basis of neighbourhoods of 0; M ⊂ R is bounded if M ⊂ aR₀ for some a ∈ k^×; x is power-bounded if {xⁿ : n ≥ 0} is bounded; R° (the power-bounded elements) is an open and integrally closed subring. (ii) An affinoid k-algebra is a pair (R, R⁺) with R a Tate k-algebra and R⁺ ⊂ R° an open integrally closed subring. (iii) (R, R⁺) is of topologically finite type (tft) if R is a quotient of k⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ = {Σ x_I T^I : x_I ∈ k, x_I → 0} and R⁺ = R°. Every Tate k-algebra and affinoid k-algebra has a completion of the same kind, and everything depends only on the completion.
items.locator: §2, Definition 2.6 and the paragraphs after it, pp. 254
items.note: Tau Ceti builds these for general Huber rings (Wedhorn §§5–6), more general than a Tate algebra over a field: IsTateRing (Huber/Basic.lean:182), IsBounded (Bounded.lean:87), powerBoundedSubring with openness and integral closedness (PowerBounded.lean:436, Basic.lean:626, PowerBounded.lean:497), Huber pairs (Pair.lean:107) and rings of integral elements (Pair.lean:73), the Tate algebra as a completed restricted power-series ring (WeightedRestrictedSeries/Completion.lean:103), and quotients of it (IsStrictlyTopologicallyFiniteType, TopologicallyFiniteType.lean:128; the tft clause R⁺ = R° is not part of that predicate).

items.name: The adic spectrum Spa(R, R⁺) and rational subsets
items.statement: For an affinoid k-algebra (R, R⁺), Spa(R, R⁺) is the set of equivalence classes of continuous valuations |·| on R with |f| ≤ 1 for all f ∈ R⁺, written f ↦ |f(x)|, topologised by the basis of rational subsets U(f_1, …, f_n / g) = {x : |f_i(x)| ≤ |g(x)| for all i}, where f_1, …, f_n generate R as an ideal and g ∈ R.
items.note: Tau Ceti defines Spa(A, A⁺) inside the continuous spectrum of a Huber ring (Spa/Basic.lean:97; Cont/Basic.lean:117) and rational subsets R(T/s) for a finite T (RationalSubset/Basic.lean:134). The generation condition for Tate rings (TA open iff T generates the unit ideal) is Wedhorn's and is used in Tau Ceti's basis results.

items.name: Adding ϖ^N to the numerators of a rational subset
items.statement: If ϖ ∈ k is topologically nilpotent and U = U(f_1, …, f_n / g) is rational, then f_{n+1} = ϖ^N can be added for N large without changing U: writing Σ h_i f_i = 1, one has ϖ^N h_i ∈ R⁺ for N large and |ϖ^N(x)| ≤ max_i |(ϖ^N h_i)(x)| |f_i(x)| ≤ |g(x)| on U. In particular |g(x)| is nonzero and bounded below on U.
items.note: Tau Ceti's rationalSubset_insert_of_forall_vle (RationalSubset/Basic.lean:203) says a numerator dominated by the denominator on R(T/s) can be adjoined without changing it; the displayed estimate supplies that hypothesis for u = ϖ^N.

items.name: Spectral spaces (Hochster)
items.statement: A topological space X is spectral if it satisfies the equivalent conditions: (i) X ≅ Spec A for some ring A; (ii) X is an inverse limit of finite T₀ spaces; (iii) X is quasicompact, has a basis of quasicompact opens stable under finite intersections, and every irreducible closed subset has a unique generic point. Spectral spaces are quasicompact, quasiseparated and T₀.
items.note: Mathlib's SpectralSpace (Mathlib/Topology/Spectral/Basic.lean:38) is form (iii), and Spec of a ring is spectral (anonymous instance, Mathlib/RingTheory/Spectrum/Prime/Topology.lean:842). Hochster's converse (i) and the inverse-limit description (ii) are planned by DiamondsAndVStacks:D0 ('prove the spectral/profinite representation results used from Hochster').

items.name: Spa(R, R⁺) is spectral; rational subsets form a basis
items.statement: For every affinoid k-algebra (R, R⁺), Spa(R, R⁺) is spectral, and the rational subsets form a basis of quasicompact open subsets stable under finite intersections.
items.note: Proved in Tau Ceti for any Huber pair (Spa/Spectral.lean:76; RationalSubset/Basis.lean:255, 197, 300).

items.name: Spa is unchanged by completion
items.statement: For an affinoid k-algebra (R, R⁺) with completion (R̂, R̂⁺), the natural map Spa(R̂, R̂⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) is a homeomorphism identifying rational subsets.
items.note: Not in Tau Ceti at the pin (Wedhorn Proposition 7.48). AdicSpaces Layer 3 needs it for its homeomorphism Spa(A_U, A_U⁺) ≅ U: Tau Ceti proves that homeomorphism only for the uncompleted localisation (spaLocalizationHomeomorph), and the pending audit of the layer records the completed case as the missing extension of valuations along the completion map.

items.name: Emptiness, units and the plus ring are detected on Spa
items.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be an affinoid k-algebra and X = Spa(R, R⁺). (i) If X = ∅ then R̂ = 0. (ii) If R is complete and |f(x)| ≠ 0 for all x ∈ X, then f is invertible. (iii) If |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ X, then f ∈ R⁺.
items.note: (i): Spa = ∅ iff A/closure{0} = 0 (Spa/Emptiness.lean:106), which forces the separated completion to vanish. (ii): the unit criterion for a complete Hausdorff Huber pair (Spa/Support.lean:144). (iii): A⁺ is the sub-unit locus, with no completeness hypothesis (Spa/Integral.lean:89).

items.name: Rational localisation R⟨f/g⟩ and its plus ring
items.statement: For a rational U = U(f_1, …, f_n / g) ⊂ Spa(R, R⁺) and R₀ as in Definition 2.6, give R[f_1/g, …, f_n/g] ⊂ R[g^{-1}] the topology with basis aR₀[f_1/g, …, f_n/g] (a ∈ k^×), let B be the integral closure of R⁺[f_1/g, …, f_n/g] in it; (R[f/g], B) is an affinoid k-algebra and (R⟨f_1/g, …, f_n/g⟩, B̂) is its completion. Spa(R⟨f/g⟩, B̂) → Spa(R, R⁺) factors over U.
items.note: Tau Ceti builds the completed topological localisation A⟨T/s⟩ (LocalizationTopology/Completion.lean:202) and a candidate plus ring (LocalizationTopology/Plus.lean:140), but openness of that plus ring is not proved at the pin, so (A_U, A_U⁺) is not yet a Huber pair there. AdicSpaces Layer 3.1 plans the construction.

items.name: Universal property of rational localisation; the presheaves 𝒪_X and 𝒪_X⁺
items.statement: For every complete affinoid k-algebra (S, S⁺) and map (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) such that Spa(S, S⁺) → Spa(R, R⁺) factors over U, there is a unique map (R⟨f/g⟩, B̂) → (S, S⁺) making the diagram commute; so the pair depends only on U. Define (𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)) = (R⟨f/g⟩, B̂) for rational U (so (𝒪_X(X), 𝒪_X⁺(X)) is the completion of (R, R⁺)), and 𝒪_X(W) = lim_{U ⊂ W rational} 𝒪_X(U) for general open W, similarly for 𝒪_X⁺.
items.locator: §2, Proposition 2.14 and the definition after it, pp. 256 (Huber [20, Proposition 1.3])
items.note: The ring-level universal property, in both the algebraic form and the geometric factor-through-U form, is in Tau Ceti (LocalizationTopology/Completion.lean:445; Spa/Localization/UniversalProperty.lean:217). A limit presheaf exists but is indexed by presentations and is explicitly not yet identified with 𝒪_X (StructurePresheaf/Basic.lean:298); the plus-ring part of the universal property waits on the plus ring (item 17). Planned by AdicSpaces Layers 3.1 and 3.3.

items.name: Stalks, valuations at points, and 𝒪_X⁺
items.statement: For x ∈ X = Spa(R, R⁺) the valuation f ↦ |f(x)| extends to 𝒪_{X,x}, and 𝒪⁺_{X,x} = {f ∈ 𝒪_{X,x} : |f(x)| ≤ 1}. 𝒪_{X,x} is local with maximal ideal {f : |f(x)| = 0}; 𝒪⁺_{X,x} is local with maximal ideal {f : |f(x)| < 1}. For every open U, 𝒪_X⁺(U) = {f ∈ 𝒪_X(U) : |f(x)| ≤ 1 for all x ∈ U}. For rational U, U ≅ Spa(𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)) compatibly with rational subsets, the presheaves and the valuations. (𝒪_X⁺ is a sheaf when 𝒪_X is; in general 𝒪_X is not known to be a sheaf.)
items.locator: §2, Proposition 2.15 and the paragraph after it, p. 257 (Huber [20, Lemma 1.5, Proposition 1.6])
items.note: AdicSpaces Layer 3.3 plans 𝒪_X⁺ and the local stalks, and Layer 3.1 the homeomorphism with U. Tau Ceti has the homeomorphism only for the uncompleted localisation (Spa/Localization/Homeomorph.lean:137) and the factorisation of a point's valuation through κ(v) (ResidueField.lean:96); stalks are absent.

items.name: Strongly noetherian Tate algebras
items.statement: A Tate k-algebra R is strongly noetherian if R⟨T_1, …, T_n⟩ = {Σ x_I T^I : x_I ∈ R̂, x_I → 0} is noetherian for all n ≥ 0. If R is of topologically finite type, R is strongly noetherian.
items.locator: §2, Definition 2.16 and the sentence after it, p. 257
items.note: The predicate is Tau Ceti's IsStronglyNoetherian (Huber/StronglyNoetherian.lean:128), stated for nonarchimedean rings. That tft algebras over a complete rank-one field are strongly noetherian needs BGR 5.2.6 (noetherianity of K⟨T⟩); the pinned docstring says it is not yet formalised, and AdicSpaces Layer 0.5 plans it.

items.name: Huber's sheaf theorem for strongly noetherian Tate algebras
items.statement: If (R, R⁺) is an affinoid k-algebra with R strongly noetherian, then 𝒪_X is a sheaf on X = Spa(R, R⁺).
items.note: AdicSpaces Layer 4.1 plans the whole chain (Wedhorn 8.28–8.35). Tau Ceti has the faithful flatness and injectivity of A → ∏ A⟨T_i/s_i⟩ for a finite rational cover of a complete strongly noetherian Tate ring (Spa/Localization/FaithfullyFlat.lean:74, 101), not the sheaf property.

items.name: The category (V), affinoid adic spaces and adic spaces over k
items.statement: (V) is the category of triples (X, 𝒪_X, (|·(x)|)_{x∈X}): a locally ringed topological space whose structure sheaf is a sheaf of complete topological k-algebras, with a continuous valuation on each stalk 𝒪_{X,x}; morphisms are morphisms of locally ringed spaces that are continuous k-algebra maps on 𝒪_X and compatible with the valuations. An affinoid adic space is an object isomorphic to the triple of an affinoid k-algebra (R, R⁺) for which 𝒪_X is a sheaf; an adic space over k is an object of (V) that is locally an affinoid adic space.
items.locator: §2, the paragraph before Definition 2.18 and Definition 2.18, pp. 257–258
items.note: AdicSpaces Layer 3.4 plans Wedhorn's pre-adic category and its sheafy subcategory 𝒱; Layer 5 plans affinoid adic spaces and adic spaces. Nothing of this is in Tau Ceti at the pin.

items.name: Maps into an affinoid adic space
items.statement: For an affinoid k-algebra (R, R⁺) with X = Spa(R, R⁺) and 𝒪_X a sheaf, and any adic space Y over k, Hom(Y, X) = Hom((R̂, R̂⁺), (𝒪_Y(Y), 𝒪_Y⁺(Y))), the continuous k-algebra maps R̂ → 𝒪_Y(Y) sending R̂⁺ into 𝒪_Y⁺(Y). Hence complete affinoid k-algebras with sheafy structure presheaf are equivalent to affinoid adic spaces.
items.locator: §2, Proposition 2.19 and the sentence after it, p. 258 (Huber [20, Proposition 2.1(ii)])
items.note: No layer states this adjunction. AdicSpaces Layer 5 defines affinoid adic spaces but does not list their universal property; AdicSpacesPartII:R0 constructs morphisms and fibre products, which rest on it. Routed there.

items.name: The points of the adic closed unit disc
items.statement: For k complete and algebraically closed, X = Spa(k⟨T⟩, k°⟨T⟩) has points of five types: (1) classical points x ∈ k°; (2), (3) the sup-norms over discs D(x, r), 0 ≤ r ≤ 1 (r ∈ |k^×|: type 2, the Gauss point for r = 1; otherwise type 3); (4) limits inf_i sup_{D_i} |f| along nested discs with empty intersection (k not spherically complete); (5) rank-two valuations Σ a_n (T − x)^n ↦ max |a_n| γ^n with γ infinitesimally close to r ∈ |k^×| from one side, one for each ray at a type-2 point. All points but those of type 2 are closed; the closure of the Gauss point is it together with the adjacent type-5 points and is homeomorphic to 𝔸¹_κ, at other type-2 points ℙ¹_κ. A type-5-like valuation with γ > 1 is continuous but violates |T| ≤ 1 on R⁺.
items.note: AdicSpaces Layer 2.4 plans the elementary points and rational subdomains of the closed unit disc (Wedhorn Example 7.57); TB.1 plans the four Berkovich types. Tau Ceti has the closed polydisc and its classical points (Spa/Polydisc.lean:72, 148), not the classification.

items.name: Huber's comparison of rigid-analytic varieties with adic spaces
items.statement: There is a fully faithful functor r : {rigid-analytic varieties over k} → {adic spaces over k}, X ↦ X^ad, with Sp(R) ↦ Spa(R, R⁺) for (R, R⁺) of tft; it induces an equivalence between quasiseparated rigid-analytic varieties and quasiseparated adic spaces locally of finite type (locally Spa of a tft pair). X ⊂ X^ad (classical points), and for quasiseparated X, U ↦ U ∩ X is a bijection from quasicompact opens of X^ad to quasicompact admissible opens of X, under which admissible covers correspond to covers; the topos of the G-topology of X is equivalent to sheaves on the sober space |X^ad|. (Example: {|x| ≤ 1} = {|x| = 1} ∪ ⋃_{r<1} {|x| ≤ r} is not admissible, because of the type-5 point.)
items.locator: §2, Theorem 2.21 and the paragraphs after it, p. 260 (Huber [22, (1.1.11)])
items.note: Planned by R1 in the AdicSpacesPartII blueprint packet (research/blueprint/packets/AdicSpacesPartII.json, review accepted): R1/rigid-analytic-space (Tate's rigid spaces, BGR 9.3.1), R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor (Huber's r_K, Sp A ↦ Spa(A, A°), classical points, admissible coverings, and for quasi-separated X the bijection between quasicompact admissible opens and quasicompact opens), R1/rigid-adic-quasi-separated-equivalence (full faithfulness and the equivalence on quasi-separated objects) and R1/rigid-adic-topos-equivalence (the topoi agree).

items.name: Formal models and the specialisation map
items.statement: For an admissible formal scheme 𝔛 over k° with Raynaud generic fibre X and adic space X^ad, there is a continuous specialisation map sp : X^ad → 𝔛 extending to a morphism of locally ringed spaces (X^ad, 𝒪⁺) → (𝔛, 𝒪_𝔛). For a quasicompact quasiseparated adic space X locally of finite type over k, formal models exist and are unique up to admissible blow-up (Raynaud), and X ≅ lim_𝔛 𝔛 as topological spaces, extending to (X, 𝒪_X⁺) ≅ lim (𝔛, 𝒪_𝔛) in locally ringed spaces. For the unit disc, starting from Spf k°⟨T⟩ and blowing up closed points recovers the type-2 points as preimages of generic points of components.
items.locator: §2, Theorem 2.22, its proof sketch and the paragraph after it, p. 261
items.note: Planned by R2 in the AdicSpacesPartII blueprint packet (research/blueprint/packets/AdicSpacesPartII.json, review accepted): R2/specialisation-map (v) gives the homeomorphism d(X) → lim |X′| over all admissible blow-ups and (d(X), O⁺) ≅ lim (X′, O_{X′}); R2/raynaud-theorem (e) gives existence of quasicompact formal models and their uniqueness up to admissible blow-up. The published proof sketch has a misprint (source issue E7).

items.name: Taut adic spaces and the equivalence with Hausdorff Berkovich spaces
items.statement: An adic space X over k is taut if it is quasiseparated and the closure of every quasicompact open is quasicompact (affinoid and qcqs adic spaces and analytifications of separated finite-type schemes are taut; Hellmann's weakly admissible locus is not). There is an equivalence of categories {Hausdorff strictly k-analytic Berkovich spaces} ≅ {taut adic spaces locally of finite type over k}, sending M(R) to Spa(R, R⁺) for (R, R⁺) of tft (taut rigid-analytic varieties give the same category).
items.locator: §2, Definition 2.23, Theorem 2.24 (first part) and the paragraphs around them, p. 262 (Huber [22, Proposition 8.3.1, Lemma 8.1.8])
items.note: Planned by H3 in the ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology blueprint packet (research/blueprint/packets/ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology--H0.json, scope H0–H3, review pending): H3/taut-spaces-and-morphisms defines tautness, and H3/berkovich-taut-comparison (a) states this equivalence, citing Sch12 Theorem 2.24 and Huber 8.3.1, 8.1.8. TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.0 plans the affinoid comparison (item 28).

items.name: Rank-one points and the maximal Hausdorff quotient
items.statement: If X_Berk corresponds to X^ad under the equivalence of Theorem 2.24, there is an injective (generally discontinuous) map of sets X_Berk → X^ad whose image is the set of rank-one valuations, and a continuous retraction X^ad → X_Berk that identifies X_Berk with the maximal Hausdorff quotient of X^ad. On the unit disc the retraction contracts each type-2 point together with its adjacent type-5 points.
items.locator: §2, Theorem 2.24 (second part) and the paragraph after it, p. 262
items.note: TB.0 plans the comparison of a strictly affinoid algebra's Berkovich spectrum with its adic spectrum by rank-one points and maximal generalisations, with continuity and the quotient topology.

items.name: The completed stalk of 𝒪⁺ is the completed valuation ring
items.statement: For x ∈ X = Spa(R, R⁺) (𝒪_X not necessarily a sheaf), with k(x) the residue field of 𝒪_{X,x} and k(x)⁺ the image of 𝒪⁺_{X,x}, and ϖ ∈ k topologically nilpotent: the ϖ-adic completion of 𝒪⁺_{X,x} equals the ϖ-adic completion of k(x)⁺, because the kernel of 𝒪⁺_{X,x} → k(x)⁺ (equal to the kernel of 𝒪_{X,x} → k(x)) is ϖ-divisible.
items.note: Used for Corollary 6.7(ii). P2 plans completed residue fields and their plus rings; the stalks themselves are AdicSpaces Layer 3.3.

items.name: Affinoid fields
items.statement: An affinoid field is a pair (K, K⁺) of a nonarchimedean field K and an open valuation subring K⁺ ⊂ K° (equivalently K with a continuous valuation up to equivalence). (k(x), k(x)⁺) is an affinoid field; completions of affinoid fields are affinoid fields; affinoid fields containing k are affinoid k-algebras.
items.locator: §2, Definition 2.26 and the paragraph after it, p. 263
items.note: A1 plans field pairs (K, K⁺), higher-rank valuation subrings included, as test objects and points; P2 plans the completed residue fields and their plus rings. Mathlib's ValuationSubring and Valued supply the ingredients.

items.name: Points of Spa as maps to complete affinoid fields
items.statement: For an affinoid k-algebra (R, R⁺), the points of Spa(R, R⁺) are in bijection with maps (R, R⁺) → (K, K⁺) to complete affinoid fields such that the quotient field of the image of R is dense in K.
items.note: Stated as immediate. Tau Ceti has the factorisation of a point's valuation through the residue field of its support (TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.residueFieldValuation), not the completed affinoid-field description. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII:R0, beside R0/fibre-over-point, which uses the completed residue affinoid field κ(y) and its morphism Spa κ(y) → Y (requested from the AdicSpaces anchor's Layer 5); routed there by route 4 (RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12/4; formerly to AdicEtaleGeometry:A1). That blueprint is finished and promoted, so the node must come by a packet amendment, not by the source route. It should become a prerequisite of R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres, R0/fibre-over-point and R0/maximal-point-closure-rational in place of their bare Huber (1.1.8)–(1.1.10) citations. Mark this item planned once the amendment lands.

items.name: Specialisation
items.statement: In a topological space X, x specialises to y (x ≻ y; y generalises to x) if y lies in the closure of {x}.
items.note: Mathlib's Specializes (x ⤳ y means y ∈ closure {x}; Mathlib/Topology/Defs/Filter.lean:207), with the same direction convention.

items.name: Specialisation in Spa(R, R⁺)
items.statement: Let x, y ∈ Spa(R, R⁺) correspond to (R, R⁺) → (K, K⁺) and (R, R⁺) → (L, L⁺) as in Proposition 2.27. Then x ≻ y if and only if K ≅ L as topological R-algebras and L⁺ ⊂ K⁺. The generalisations of any y form a totally ordered chain of length exactly the rank of the valuation of y. In particular the point (K, K°) of a nonarchimedean field K over R is the unique rank-one point and specialises to every other point with the same K.
items.locator: §2, Proposition 2.29 and the paragraph after it, p. 263 (Huber [22, (1.1.6)–(1.1.10)])
items.note: AdicSpaces Layer 1 develops vertical and horizontal specialisation only as far as Theorem 7.10 needs (Tau Ceti has coarsenings of valuations, TauCeti/RingTheory/Valuation/Coarsen.lean, and microbial valuations). The field-pair description of specialisation in Spa over a nonarchimedean field is not planned. Owner: AdicSpacesPartII:R0 (route 4; RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12/4; formerly to AdicEtaleGeometry:A1). R0/maximal-point-closure-rational uses Huber 1.1.10(i) (generalisations form a chain) and R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres uses 1.1.10(iii), and no node states them. As for item 31, the node must come by a packet amendment to the finished blueprint, and should become a prerequisite of those nodes. AdicEtaleGeometry's Layer-1 request for the description of Spa(K, K⁺) as a chain of specialisations (needed by A2/dimension-of-adic-spaces) should then point at it. Mark this item planned once the amendment lands.

items.name: Perfectoid field
items.statement: A perfectoid field is a complete nonarchimedean field K of residue characteristic p > 0 whose rank-one valuation is nondiscrete and such that Frobenius is surjective on K°/p (Definition 1.2 phrases the same with K° the power-bounded elements). The nondiscreteness excludes the unramified extensions of ℚ_p.
items.note: Planned by P1 (decomposition node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-field-definition, which also records the equivalence with ECD Definition 3.6 / Proposition 3.8). Neither library defines perfectoid fields.

items.name: The value group of a perfectoid field is p-divisible
items.statement: Let |·| : K → Γ ∪ {0} be the rank-one valuation of a perfectoid field K with Γ = |K^×| minimal. Then Γ is p-divisible. (Proof: Γ is generated by the |x| with |p| < |x| ≤ 1; for such x choose y with |x − y^p| ≤ |p|, so |y|^p = |x|.)

items.name: Perfectoid fields of characteristic p are the complete perfect nonarchimedean fields
items.statement: A nonarchimedean field of characteristic p is a perfectoid field if and only if it is complete and perfect.
items.note: Stated without proof. Planned by P1 (node perfectoid-field-definition). Mathlib has perfect rings (PerfectRing, Mathlib/FieldTheory/Perfect.lean:44).

items.name: Perfectoid fields are the complete deeply ramified fields of rank one
items.statement: With the definition of deeply ramified fields of Gabber–Ramero [15], a perfectoid field is deeply ramified, and conversely a complete deeply ramified field with a valuation of rank one is perfectoid ([15, Proposition 6.6.6]).
items.note: Enters only the first ('ramification theory') proof of Theorem 3.7; the P3 node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields records Gabber–Ramero Propositions 6.3.6, 6.6.2 and 6.6.6 as its inputs for that proof. The atlas has no stage on deeply ramified fields as such.

items.name: The tilt as a multiplicative limit and Fontaine's sharp map
items.statement: Let K be perfectoid and ϖ ∈ K^× with |p| ≤ |ϖ| < 1. Projection gives a multiplicative homeomorphism lim_{x↦x^p} K° ≅ lim_Φ K°/ϖ (inverse-limit topologies; each K°/ϖ discrete); in particular the right side is independent of ϖ. The map lim_Φ K°/ϖ → K°, x ↦ x♯ = lim_n x̃_n^{p^n} for arbitrary lifts x̃_n ∈ K° of x_n, is well defined, multiplicative and continuous, and x ↦ (x♯, (x^{1/p})♯, …) inverts the projection.
items.note: Mathlib's PreTilt O p = Perfection(O/p) is the case ϖ = p, and PreTilt.untilt is the multiplicative sharp map (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/Untilt.lean:49); the ϖ-version, the topology and the homeomorphism with lim_{x↦x^p} K° are planned by P1 (node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field).

items.name: The tilt K♭ of a perfectoid field
items.statement: (ii) There is ϖ♭ ∈ lim_Φ K°/ϖ with |(ϖ♭)♯| = |ϖ|; set K♭ = (lim_Φ K°/ϖ)[(ϖ♭)^{-1}]. (iii) There is a multiplicative homeomorphism K♭ ≅ lim_{x↦x^p} K, giving x ↦ x♯ : K♭ → K; K♭ is a perfectoid field of characteristic p with K♭° = lim_{x↦x^p} K° ≅ lim_Φ K°/ϖ, its rank-one valuation is |x|_{K♭} = |x♯|_K, |K♭^×| = |K^×|, K♭°/ϖ♭ ≅ K°/ϖ and K♭°/m♭ = K°/m. (iv) If K has characteristic p then K♭ = K. Remark 3.5: replacing ϖ by (ϖ♭)♯ one may assume ϖ has a compatible system of p^n-th roots ϖ^{1/p^n} = ((ϖ♭)^{1/p^n})♯, and such a system determines ϖ♭.
items.note: Mathlib's Tilt (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfection.lean:826) is the fraction field of PreTilt O p for a valued field, 'as defined in Perfectoid Spaces'; its valuation, perfectoidness and the listed identifications are planned by P1 (node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-field).

items.name: Continuous valuations of K and K♭ correspond
items.statement: For a perfectoid field K with tilt K♭, |·| ↦ |·|♭ with |x|♭ = |x♯| is a bijection between continuous valuations of K up to equivalence and continuous valuations of K♭ up to equivalence. (Proof: |x + y|♭ = lim |(x^{1/p^n})♯ + (y^{1/p^n})♯|^{p^n}; continuous valuations correspond to open valuation subrings K⁺ ⊂ K°, i.e. to valuation subrings of K°/m = K♭°/m♭.)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/continuous-valuations-under-tilting.

items.name: Finite extensions of perfectoid fields are perfectoid
items.statement: Let K be a perfectoid field and L a finite extension of K. Then L, with its natural topology as a finite-dimensional K-vector space, is a perfectoid field.
items.locator: §3, Theorem 3.7(i), p. 267; proof at the end of §5, p. 283
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields. Proved via Theorem 5.25 (S = L perfectoid when L is in the essential image), which the proof of (ii) shows is everything.

items.name: Tilting of finite extensions of a perfectoid field
items.statement: Let K be perfectoid with tilt K♭. The functor L ↦ L♭ is an equivalence between finite extensions of K and finite extensions of K♭, preserving degrees. Two proofs: (a) by ramification theory, Gabber–Ramero Propositions 6.6.2, 6.6.6 (L°a/K°a étale) and 6.3.6 (finite projective); (b) reducing to K♭ algebraically closed: for M the completion of an algebraic closure of K♭ and M♯ its untilt (algebraically closed by Lemma 5.21 and Proposition 3.8), the union N of the L♯ for finite L/K♭ inside M is dense and, by Krasner's lemma, algebraically closed; so every finite F/K lies in some Galois L♯ with Gal(L♯/K) = Gal(L/K♭), and F = ((L)^H)♯.
items.locator: §3, Theorem 3.7(ii), p. 267; both proofs at the end of §5, p. 283
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields, whose gap list records Krasner's lemma and the density of N as standard inputs; Mathlib has Krasner's lemma for complete (normal) fields (IsKrasner, Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Field/Krasner.lean:56). This is Fontaine–Wintenberger's theorem for these fields.

items.name: If K♭ is algebraically closed, so is K
items.statement: Let K be perfectoid with tilt K♭. If K♭ is algebraically closed, then K is algebraically closed. (Proof by successive approximation: for monic irreducible P ∈ K°[X] with |a_0| = 1 (possible as |K^×| = |K♭^×| is a ℚ-vector space), lift P mod ϖ to Q over K♭° with a root y; then ϖ | P(y♯), and P_1(X) = c^{-d} P(cX + y♯) with |c|^d = |P(y♯)| is again integral; iterate.)
items.note: Part of node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-extensions-of-perfectoid-fields ("Auxiliary: if K♭ is algebraically closed then K is algebraically closed").

items.name: Almost zero elements and modules over K°
items.statement: Fix a perfectoid field K and m = K°° = {x : |x| < 1}, the maximal ideal of K°. An element x of a K°-module M is almost zero if m x = 0; M is almost zero if m M = 0.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-modules-over-perfectoid-base. P0 generalises to an abstract base (V, 𝔪) with 𝔪 idempotent and flat.

items.name: Almost zero modules form a thick subcategory
items.statement: The full subcategory of almost zero K°-modules is thick (closed under subobjects, quotients and extensions); for an extension 0 → M′ → M → M″ → 0 with m M′ = m M″ = 0 one gets m² M = 0, and m² = m.
items.note: Mathlib's IsSerreClass is the closure condition; the instance for almost zero modules is not stated. m² = m uses that the valuation is nondiscrete (not justified in the paper; recorded by the decomposition review, not re-recorded here).

items.name: The category of almost K°-modules
items.statement: K°a-mod = K°-mod/(m-torsion), with the localisation functor M ↦ M^a whose kernel is exactly the thick subcategory of almost zero modules; K°-mod → K°a-mod → K-mod composes to passage to the generic fibre.
items.locator: §4, the sequence of localisation functors and Definition 4.3, p. 268
items.note: Mathlib's Serre-quotient localisation is abelian for any Serre class (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Abelian/SerreClass/Localization.lean:417); the almost category itself is planned by P0.

items.name: Hom in the almost category
items.statement: For K°-modules M, N: Hom_{K°a}(M^a, N^a) = Hom_{K°}(m ⊗ M, N). Hence Hom_{K°a}(X, Y) is naturally a K°-module without almost zero elements, and alHom(X, Y) := Hom(X, Y)^a.

items.name: K°a-mod is an abelian tensor category with internal Hom
items.statement: K°a-mod is an abelian tensor category, kernels, cokernels and tensor products being the unique ones compatible with K°-mod (M^a ⊗ N^a = (M ⊗ N)^a), and Hom(L, alHom(M, N)) = Hom(L ⊗ M, N) functorially. So K°a-algebras and modules over them are defined as usual; a K°-algebra R gives a K°a-algebra R^a, and R-modules give R^a-modules.
items.locator: §4, Proposition 4.5 and the paragraph after it, p. 269 (Gabber–Ramero [15, §2.2.6, §2.2.12])

items.name: Almost elements: the right adjoint M ↦ M_*
items.statement: The localisation functor M ↦ M^a has a right adjoint M ↦ M_* = Hom_{K°a}(K°a, M) (almost elements); (M_*)^a → M is an isomorphism, and (M^a)_* = Hom(m, M) for a K°-module M. For a K°a-algebra A, A_* is a K°-algebra with (A_*)^a = A; every A-module comes from an A_*-module, A-modules form an abelian tensor category, and A-algebras are K°a-algebras with an algebra map from A.
items.locator: §4, Proposition 4.6 and the paragraph after it, p. 269 (Gabber–Ramero [15, Proposition 2.2.14])

items.name: Flat, almost projective, almost finitely generated and presented modules
items.statement: Let A be a K°a-algebra. (i) An A-module M is flat if X ↦ M ⊗_A X is exact; for a K°-algebra R and R-module N, N^a is flat over R^a iff Tor_i^R(N, X) is almost zero for all R-modules X and i > 0. (ii) M is almost projective if X ↦ alHom_A(M, X) is exact; N^a is almost projective iff Ext^i_R(N, X) is almost zero for all X and i > 0. (iii) N^a is almost finitely generated (resp. presented) if for every ε ∈ m there is a finitely generated (resp. presented) R-module N_ε and f_ε : N_ε → N with kernel and cokernel killed by ε; uniformly almost finitely generated if the N_ε can be generated by a fixed number n of elements. (Remark 4.8: these depend only on N^a; K°a is in general not projective for Hom, as K° → Hom(m, K°/ϖ) misses Σ ϖ^{1−1/p^i} x_i.)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P0/almost-finite-projective-and-finite-etale-algebras; Mathlib has only the ordinary notions.

items.name: An almost finitely presented extension of rings of integers
items.statement: Let K be the p-adic completion of ℚ_p(p^{1/p^∞}), p ≠ 2, and L = K(p^{1/2}). Then L°a is an almost finitely presented, indeed uniformly almost finitely generated, K°a-module: for n ≥ 1 the injection K° ⊕ p^{1/(2p^n)} K° → L° has cokernel killed by p^{1/(2p^n)}.
items.note: Listed among the sources of the P0 node on almost finite projective algebras.

items.name: Finite projective almost modules
items.statement: For a K°a-algebra A, an A-module M is flat and almost finitely presented if and only if it is almost projective and almost finitely generated. Such M are called finite projective; uniformly finite projective if moreover uniformly almost finitely generated.
items.locator: §4, Proposition 4.10 and the paragraph after it, p. 270 (Gabber–Ramero [15, Proposition 2.4.18])

items.name: Rank decomposition of a uniformly finite projective module
items.statement: For a K°a-algebra A and a uniformly finite projective A-module M there is a unique decomposition A = A_0 × A_1 × ⋯ × A_k such that M_i = M ⊗_A A_i has Λ^i M_i invertible and Λ^{i+1} M_i = 0; an A-module L is invertible if L ⊗_A alHom_A(L, A) = A.

items.name: Unramified, étale and finite étale almost algebras
items.statement: For a K°a-algebra A and an A-algebra B with multiplication μ : B ⊗_A B → B: A → B is unramified if there is e ∈ (B ⊗_A B)_* with e² = e, μ(e) = 1 and x e = 0 for all x ∈ ker(μ)_*; étale if unramified and B is flat over A; finite étale if étale and B is almost finitely presented over A (then B is finite projective). A_fét denotes the finite étale A-algebras.
items.note: Mathlib has the ordinary notions (with the diagonal idempotent for finite unramified algebras, Algebra.FormallyUnramified.lmul_elem); the almost versions are the P0 node on almost finite étale algebras.

items.name: Duals, trace and the trace form of a finite projective almost algebra
items.statement: For a finite projective A-module P, P* = alHom(P, A) is finite projective, P** ≅ P, End(P)^a = P ⊗_A P*, giving tr_{P/A} : End(P)^a → A. For an A-algebra B finite projective as a module, the trace form t_{B/A} : B ⊗_A B → A is μ followed by b ↦ tr(b′ ↦ bb′) (made precise via B_* → End_{A_*}(B_*) since almost objects have no elements, Remark 4.15).
items.locator: §4, the paragraph before Definition 4.14, Definition 4.14 and Remark 4.15, pp. 271–272

items.name: Finite étale almost algebras are those with perfect trace pairing
items.statement: In the situation of Definition 4.14, A → B is finite étale if and only if the trace form is a perfect pairing, i.e. induces B ≅ B*.

items.name: Finite étale almost algebras lift uniquely along ϖ-adically complete flat bases
items.statement: Let A be a K°a-algebra that is flat over K°a and ϖ-adically complete (A ≅ lim A/ϖⁿ). Then B ↦ B ⊗_A A/ϖ is an equivalence A_fét ≅ (A/ϖ)_fét; every B ∈ A_fét is flat over K°a and ϖ-adically complete; and B is uniformly finite projective over A iff B ⊗_A A/ϖ is uniformly finite projective over A/ϖ.
items.locator: §4, Theorem 4.17 and proof, p. 272 (first part: Gabber–Ramero [15, Theorem 5.3.27])
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P0/finite-etale-lifting-along-complete-flat-almost-algebras. The proof's 'the rest is easy' hides an almost-Nakayama argument for the uniformity clause (source issue E6, already recorded in the atlas as PerfectoidSpaces/E4).

items.name: Perfectoid K-algebras
items.statement: A perfectoid K-algebra is a Banach K-algebra R whose power-bounded elements R° ⊂ R form an open and bounded subset and such that Frobenius Φ : R°/ϖ → R°/ϖ is surjective; morphisms are continuous K-algebra maps (Definition 1.6: equivalently Φ surjective on R°/p). K-Perf denotes this category.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/perfectoid-tate-rings-and-algebras (which also carries the Tate-ring generalisation of ECD 3.1).

items.name: Perfectoid K°a-algebras and K°a/ϖ-algebras
items.statement: (ii) A perfectoid K°a-algebra is a ϖ-adically complete flat K°a-algebra A on which Frobenius induces an isomorphism A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A/ϖ. (iii) A perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebra is a flat K°a/ϖ-algebra A on which Frobenius induces an isomorphism A/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A. Morphisms are those of K°a-, resp. K°a/ϖ-algebras; categories K°a-Perf and (K°a/ϖ)-Perf.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary.

items.name: The tilting equivalence K-Perf ≅ K♭-Perf
items.statement: The categories of perfectoid K-algebras and perfectoid K♭-algebras are equivalent, through K-Perf ≅ K°a-Perf ≅ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf = (K♭°a/ϖ♭)-Perf ≅ K♭°a-Perf ≅ K♭-Perf (the middle identification because K°/ϖ = K♭°/ϖ♭). Theorem 1.7: a perfectoid K-algebra R goes to R♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R, and there is a map R♭ → R, f ↦ f♯.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt. P1 also plans the Tate-ring version (ECD 3.13), for which Sch12 gives no proof.

items.name: Flatness and completeness of almost modules via almost elements
items.statement: Let M be a K°a-module. (i) M is flat over K°a iff M_* is flat over K° iff M_* has no ϖ-torsion. (ii) If N is a flat K°-module and M = N^a, then M is flat and M_* = {x ∈ N[1/ϖ] : εx ∈ N for all ε ∈ m}. (iii) If M is flat, then (xM)_* = x M_* for x ∈ K°, M_*/xM_* ⊂ (M/xM)_*, and for every ε ∈ m the image of (M/xεM)_* in (M/xM)_* is M_*/xM_* (Remark 5.4: the non-surjectivity comes from elements as in Remark 4.8). (iv) If M is flat, M is ϖ-adically complete iff M_* is.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/almost-integral-dictionary.

items.name: The almost integral structure of a perfectoid K-algebra
items.statement: For a perfectoid K-algebra R, Φ induces an isomorphism R°/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ R°/ϖ, and A = R°a is a perfectoid K°a-algebra.

items.name: From perfectoid K°a-algebras back to perfectoid K-algebras
items.statement: Let A be a perfectoid K°a-algebra and R = A_*[ϖ^{-1}], a Banach K-algebra with A_* open and bounded. Then A_* = R° is the set of power-bounded elements, R is perfectoid, and Φ : A_*/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ A_*/ϖ. Lemma 5.7 (in the proof): if x ∈ R and x^p ∈ A_*, then x ∈ A_*. Hence K°a-Perf ≅ K-Perf.

items.name: Perfectoid K-algebras are reduced
items.statement: Every perfectoid K-algebra R is reduced (a nonzero nilpotent x would give Kx ⊂ R°, contradicting boundedness of R°).

items.name: In characteristic p, perfectoid means perfect
items.statement: Let K have characteristic p and R a Banach K-algebra with R° open and bounded. Then R is perfectoid if and only if R is perfect.

items.name: Perfectoid K°a-algebras are determined by their reduction mod ϖ
items.statement: A ↦ Ā = A/ϖ is an equivalence K°a-Perf ≅ (K°a/ϖ)-Perf: a perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebra admits a unique compatible system of flat (K°/ϖⁿ)^a-algebras Ā_n with Ā_n/ϖ^{n−1} ≅ Ā_{n−1}, all obstructions and ambiguities vanishing because L^a_{Ā_n/(K°/ϖⁿ)^a} = 0 (by induction, via the triangle induced from 0 → Ā → Ā_n → Ā_{n−1} → 0); the limit is perfectoid.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/deformation-lifting-of-perfectoid-mod-varpi-algebras. The triangle is cited as Gabber–Ramero 'Theorem 2.5.36' in the book numbering; the node records that the arXiv numbering differs.

items.name: The cotangent complex (Quillen, Illusie)
items.statement: To a ring map R → S one attaches L_{S/R} ∈ D^{≤0}(S), defined via a simplicial resolution S_• of S by free R-algebras as the object of D^{≤0}(S) of the simplicial S-module Ω¹_{S_•/R} ⊗_{S_•} S (Dold–Kan). H⁰(L_{S/R}) = Ω¹_{S/R}; for R → S → T there is a triangle T ⊗^L_S L_{S/R} → L_{T/R} → L_{T/S} → extending T ⊗_S Ω¹_{S/R} → Ω¹_{T/R} → Ω¹_{T/S} → 0; for R → S smooth, L_{S/R} is Ω¹_{S/R} in degree 0.
items.note: DD.0 plans the cotangent complex with transitivity and the smooth computation; Mathlib has only Kähler differentials and the naive cotangent complex (Algebra.H1Cotangent).

items.name: Obstructions to flat deformations along a square-zero extension
items.statement: Let I ⊂ R with I² = 0, R_0 = R/I and S_0 a flat R_0-algebra. There is an obstruction class in Ext²(L_{S_0/R_0}, S_0 ⊗_{R_0} I) vanishing exactly when there is a flat R-algebra S with S ⊗_R R_0 = S_0; if deformations exist, their isomorphism classes form a torsor under Ext¹(L_{S_0/R_0}, S_0 ⊗_{R_0} I), and each deformation has automorphism group Hom(L_{S_0/R_0}, S_0 ⊗_{R_0} I) (isomorphisms restricting to the identity on S_0).
items.locator: §5, Theorem 5.11 and the sentence after it, p. 277 (Illusie [23, III.2.1.2.3]; Gabber–Ramero [15, Proposition 3.2.9])
items.note: SF.4 plans infinitesimal lifting and obstruction complexes, DD.0 the cotangent complex. The almost version used in Theorem 5.10 is item item 72.

items.name: Obstructions to lifting morphisms along a square-zero extension
items.statement: For flat R-algebras S, S′ with reductions S_0, S′_0 to R_0 and f_0 : S_0 → S′_0, there is an obstruction class in Ext¹(L_{S_0/R_0}, S′_0 ⊗_{R_0} I) vanishing exactly when f_0 lifts to f : S → S′; the lifts then form a torsor under Hom(L_{S_0/R_0}, S′_0 ⊗_{R_0} I).

items.name: The cotangent complex of a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra vanishes
items.statement: (i) For a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra R, L_{R/𝔽_p} ≅ 0. (ii) For a map R → S of 𝔽_p-algebras such that the relative Frobenius induces an isomorphism R_(Φ) ⊗^L_R S → S_(Φ) in D(R), L_{S/R} ≅ 0. (Proof of (ii): on a free simplicial resolution the relative Frobenius is a quasi-isomorphism inducing R_(Φ) ⊗^L L_{S/R} ≅ L_{S_(Φ)/R_(Φ)}, and it kills dX_i ↦ dX_i^p = 0.)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi; DD.0 supplies L.

items.name: Witt vectors of a perfect ring as its unique deformation
items.statement: Since L_{R/𝔽_p} = 0 for a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra R (and already Ω¹_{R/𝔽_p} = 0, as d(y^p) = p y^{p−1} dy = 0), W(R) can be defined as the unique deformation of R to a flat p-adically complete ℤ_p-algebra.
items.note: Planned by P1 in the PerfectoidSpaces blueprint packet (research/blueprint/packets/PerfectoidSpaces--P0.json, 324 nodes over P0–P7): an acceptance criterion of PerfectoidSpaces:P1/cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi is that W(R) is the unique flat p-adically complete deformation of a perfect R (Sch12 Remark 5.14; Bhatt Example 6.1.6), and part (a) of that node proves L_{R/𝔽_p} ≃ 0 for perfect R. Mathlib has W(R) (WittVector) with Teichmüller representatives, not the uniqueness.

items.name: The almost cotangent complex and almost deformation theory
items.statement: Gabber–Ramero: for a map R → S of K°-algebras, L^a_{S/R} ∈ D(S^a) depends only on R^a → S^a, which defines L^a_{B/A} ∈ D^{≤0}(B) for K°a-algebras A → B (Remark 5.15: in [15] L_{B/A} lives over an actual ring; the almost version suffices); Theorems 5.11–5.12 and Proposition 5.13 remain true in the almost setting.
items.locator: §5, the paragraph after the proof of Proposition 5.13 and Remark 5.15, p. 278
items.note: The decomposition's gap 'Almost deformation theory and cotangent-complex inputs cited from Gabber-Ramero' is attached to the P1 nodes on deformation lifting and cotangent vanishing.

items.name: The almost cotangent complex of a perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebra vanishes
items.statement: For a perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebra Ā, L^a_{Ā/(K°a/ϖ)} ≅ 0 (by the almost version of Proposition 5.13, or via the flat K°/ϖ-algebra B = (Ā × K°a/ϖ)_{!!} with B/ϖ^{1/p} ≅ B via Φ).

items.name: The explicit tilt of a perfectoid K-algebra
items.statement: For perfectoid R with A = R°a, put A♭ = lim_Φ A/ϖ (a K♭°a-algebra via K♭°a = lim_Φ K°a/ϖ) and R♭ = A♭_*[(ϖ♭)^{-1}]. Then R♭ is a perfectoid K♭-algebra with perfectoid K♭°a-algebra A♭, and it is the tilt of R; moreover R♭ = lim_{x↦x^p} R, A♭_* = lim_{x↦x^p} A_*, A♭_*/ϖ♭ ≅ A_*/ϖ, and there is a continuous multiplicative map R♭ → R, x ↦ x♯. The tilting functor is independent of ϖ and ϖ♭ (Remark 5.18).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilting-equivalence-and-explicit-tilt.

items.name: The untilting functor through Fontaine's θ
items.statement: The inverse of tilting is R = W(R♭°) ⊗_{W(K♭°)} K, using θ : W(K♭°) → K; a direct proof of the tilting equivalence along these lines avoids almost mathematics (cf. Kedlaya–Liu).
items.note: P1 plans θ, its kernel and the classification of untilts (nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P1/fontaine-theta-and-primitive-kernel and untilts-classified-by-primitive-ideals). Mathlib's fontaineTheta (Mathlib/RingTheory/Perfectoid/FontaineTheta.lean:165) is θ on the p-adic tilt for a p-adically complete ring, with surjectivity when Frobenius is surjective mod p (line 195).

items.name: The perfectoid closed polydisc and its tilt
items.statement: R = K⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ = (K°⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩)[ϖ^{-1}] is a perfectoid K-algebra with R° the ϖ-adic completion of K°[T_i^{1/p^∞}], and its tilt is R♭ = K♭⟨T_1^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩.
items.note: P1's tests include perfected Tate balls and tori.

items.name: Tilting preserves perfectoid fields
items.statement: A perfectoid K-algebra R is a perfectoid field iff R♭ is. (R is a perfectoid field iff its spectral norm ‖x‖_R = inf{|t|^{-1} : t ∈ K^×, tx ∈ R°} is multiplicative; ‖x‖_{R♭} = ‖x♯‖_R.)

items.name: Finite étale algebras over perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebras are perfectoid
items.statement: If Ā is a perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebra and B̄ a finite étale Ā-algebra, then B̄ is a perfectoid K°a/ϖ-algebra (Frobenius by Gabber–Ramero [15, Theorem 3.5.13(ii)]). Consequently A_fét → R_fét and A♭_fét → R♭_fét are fully faithful, in the diagram R_fét ← A_fét ≅ Ā_fét ≅ A♭_fét → R♭_fét over the tilting chain.
items.locator: §5, Proposition 5.22 and the diagram after it, p. 281
items.note: Nodes PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p and tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful.

items.name: Almost purity in characteristic p
items.statement: If K has characteristic p, R is a perfectoid K-algebra and S/R is finite étale (with the canonical topology), then S is perfectoid, S°a is finite étale over R°a, and S°a is a uniformly finite projective R°a-module.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/finite-etale-covers-in-characteristic-p. The proof starts from "some finitely generated R°-subalgebra S_0 with S_0 ⊗ K = S" and uses that its elements are integral over R°, which needs S_0 finite as an R°-module (source issue E10).

items.name: The canonical topology on finitely generated modules over A[t^{-1}]
items.statement: If t ∈ A is a nonzerodivisor, every finitely generated A[t^{-1}]-module M has a canonical topology giving each finitely generated A-submodule the t-adic topology; all maps of finitely generated A[t^{-1}]-modules are continuous; if A is complete and M projective, M is complete. So a finite étale S over a perfectoid R has a canonical complete topology.
items.note: A1 plans the canonical topology on a finite (étale) algebra over a complete Tate pair. Mathlib's IsModuleTopology gives a canonical topology on modules; Tau Ceti proves uniqueness and completeness of the module topology on finite modules over a complete Hausdorff noetherian Tate ring (OpenMapping.lean:306), which does not cover perfectoid rings.

items.name: Tilting of finite étale algebras is fully faithful
items.statement: For a perfectoid K-algebra R with tilt R♭ there is a fully faithful functor R♭_fét → R_fét inverse to tilting; its essential image consists of the finite étale S/R such that S (with its natural topology) is perfectoid and S°a is finite étale over R°a; then S°a is a uniformly finite projective R°a-module, and the functor preserves degrees. All finite étale algebras over A, Ā or A♭ are uniformly almost finitely presented.
items.locator: §5, the diagram before Theorem 5.25, Theorem 5.25 and the sentence after it, pp. 282–283
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/tilting-finite-etale-algebras-fully-faithful.

items.name: Perfectoid affinoid K-algebras
items.statement: A perfectoid affinoid K-algebra is an affinoid K-algebra (R, R⁺) with R a perfectoid K-algebra. Then m R° ⊂ R⁺ ⊂ R° (topologically nilpotent elements lie in the integrally closed R⁺), so R⁺ is almost equal to R°.
items.locator: §6, Definition 6.1 and the sentence after it, p. 283
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P1/tilt-of-perfectoid-tate-ring cites Definition 6.1 and Lemma 6.2.

items.name: Tilting perfectoid affinoid algebras
items.statement: The categories of perfectoid affinoid K-algebras and perfectoid affinoid K♭-algebras are equivalent; if (R, R⁺) ↦ (R♭, R♭⁺), then x ↦ x♯ induces R♭⁺/ϖ♭ ≅ R⁺/ϖ, and R♭⁺ = lim_{x↦x^p} R⁺. (Open integrally closed subrings of R° correspond to integrally closed subrings of R°/m, compatibly with tilting.)

items.name: The tilting homeomorphism of adic spectra
items.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra with tilt (R♭, R♭⁺), X = Spa(R, R⁺), X♭ = Spa(R♭, R♭⁺). Then x ↦ x♭, |f(x♭)| = |f♯(x)|, is a homeomorphism X ≅ X♭ identifying rational subsets (Theorem 6.3(i), Theorem 1.8(i), Corollary 6.7(iii)). The map is well defined by the proof of Proposition 3.6 and continuous because the preimage of U(f_1, …, f_n / g) is U(f_1♯, …, f_n♯ / g♯) when f_n is a power of ϖ♭; injectivity and the rational-subset statement follow from the approximation lemma, surjectivity from untilting the completed residue fields and their valuations.
items.locator: §6, Theorem 6.3(i), the start of its proof and Corollary 6.7(iii), pp. 284–285, 290–291; §1, Theorem 1.8(i), p. 248
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets.

items.name: Explicit perfectoid structure of rational localisations
items.statement: Let U = U(f_1, …, f_n / g) ⊂ Spa(R♭, R♭⁺) be rational with preimage U♯ ⊂ Spa(R, R⁺), f_i, g ∈ R♭° and f_n = (ϖ♭)^N. (i) The ϖ-adic completion R°⟨(f_1♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}, …, (f_n♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}⟩ of the subring R°[(f_i♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}] ⊂ R[1/g♯], made almost, is a perfectoid K°a-algebra. (ii) 𝒪_X(U♯) is a perfectoid K-algebra with 𝒪_X(U♯)°a = R°⟨(f_i♯/g♯)^{1/p^∞}⟩^a. (iii) The tilt of 𝒪_X(U♯) is 𝒪_{X♭}(U).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/rational-localization-of-perfectoid-affinoids. The proof first treats characteristic p (the ideal I generated by T_i^{1/p^m} g^{1/p^m} − f_i^{1/p^m} is perfect) and then transports mod ϖ through the tilt.

items.name: The approximation lemma
items.statement: Let R = K⟨T_0^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩ and f ∈ R° homogeneous of degree d ∈ ℤ[1/p]. For every rational c ≥ 0 and ε > 0 there is g_{c,ε} ∈ R♭° = K♭°⟨T_0^{1/p^∞}, …, T_n^{1/p^∞}⟩, homogeneous of degree d, with |f(x) − g♯_{c,ε}(x)| ≤ |ϖ|^{1−ε} max(|f(x)|, |ϖ|^c) for all x ∈ Spa(R, R°). For ε < 1 this gives max(|f(x)|, |ϖ|^c) = max(|g♯_{c,ε}(x)|, |ϖ|^c) (Remark 6.6). The proof is an explicit induction c ↦ c + a (0 < a < ε in ℤ[1/p]) with a shrinking error ε(c), writing f − g_c♯ on {|f| ≤ |ϖ|^c} through Lemma 6.4 as a convergent sum of homogeneous terms ϖ^{c+1−ε+ε(c′)} (g_c♯/ϖ^c)^i r_i and correcting g_c by the tilted sum.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma. The same lemma drives Proposition 8.7 (item item 133).

items.name: Approximation on a general perfectoid affinoid
items.statement: For a perfectoid affinoid (R, R⁺), every f ∈ R and all c ≥ 0, ε > 0 there is g_{c,ε} ∈ R♭ with |f(x) − g♯_{c,ε}(x)| ≤ |ϖ|^{1−ε} max(|f(x)|, |ϖ|^c) for all x ∈ Spa(R, R⁺) (reduce to R⁺ = R° and maximal points, write f = g_0♯ + ϖ g_1♯ + ⋯ + ϖ^c g_c♯ and apply Lemma 6.5 to T_0 + ϖT_1 + ⋯ + ϖ^cT_c).

items.name: Completed residue fields of a perfectoid affinoid are perfectoid
items.statement: For every x ∈ X = Spa(R, R⁺) with (R, R⁺) perfectoid affinoid, the completed residue field k(x)^ is a perfectoid field.
items.note: Proved first in characteristic p via Proposition 2.25, then in general after the homeomorphism (iii).

items.name: Rational localisations of perfectoid affinoids and their tilts
items.statement: For every rational U ⊂ X = Spa(R, R⁺) (R, R⁺ perfectoid affinoid), (𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)) is a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra with tilt (𝒪_{X♭}(U♭), 𝒪⁺_{X♭}(U♭)) (Theorem 6.3(ii), Theorem 1.8(ii)); it is characterised by the universal property of Proposition 2.14 among perfectoid affinoid K-algebras, and tilting that property gives the tilt.
items.locator: §6, Corollary 6.8 and proof, p. 291; Theorem 6.3(ii), p. 284
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/tilting-homeomorphism-and-rational-subsets.

items.name: p-finite perfectoid affinoid algebras
items.statement: For K of characteristic p, a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra (R, R⁺) is p-finite if it is the completed perfection of a reduced affinoid K-algebra (S, S⁺) of topologically finite type: R⁺ is the ϖ-adic completion of lim_Φ S⁺ and R = R⁺[ϖ^{-1}].
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/p-finite-acyclicity-from-tate. By Definition 2.6(iii), "topologically finite type" includes S⁺ = S°.

items.name: Reduced affinoid algebras of topologically finite type
items.statement: Let (S, S⁺) be a reduced affinoid K-algebra of topologically finite type and X = Spa(S, S⁺). (i) S⁺ = S° ⊂ S is open and bounded. (ii) For every rational U ⊂ X, (𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)) is reduced and of topologically finite type. (iii) For every cover of X by finitely many rational subsets U_i, every cohomology group of 0 → 𝒪_X(X)° → ∏ 𝒪_X(U_i)° → ∏ 𝒪_X(U_i ∩ U_j)° → ⋯ is killed by a power of ϖ.
items.locator: §6, Proposition 6.10 and proof, pp. 291–292 (BGR [2] 6.2.4 Theorem 1, 7.3.2 Corollary 10, 8.2.1 Theorem 1; Huber [20, Proposition 4.3])
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/p-finite-acyclicity-from-tate. (iii) follows from Tate's acyclicity (item 92) by the open mapping theorem (item 93). The atlas's source issue PerfectoidSpaces/E13 calls '(i) S⁺ = S°' a misprint; with Definition 2.6(iii), tft includes S⁺ = S°, so the printed statement is correct.

items.name: Tate's acyclicity theorem
items.statement: For an affinoid K-algebra of topologically finite type and a finite cover of X = Spa(S, S⁺) by rational subsets, the augmented Čech complex 0 → 𝒪_X(X) → ∏ 𝒪_X(U_i) → ∏ 𝒪_X(U_i ∩ U_j) → ⋯ is exact.
items.note: AdicSpaces Layer 4 plans exactness in every degree of the augmented Čech complex for strongly noetherian Tate rings and recovers Tate's acyclicity for the closed disc.

items.name: Banach's open mapping theorem
items.statement: A continuous linear surjection between Banach spaces over a complete nonarchimedean field is open; used to show that the subspace and quotient topologies on ker d_i = im d_{i−1} of the Čech complex agree.
items.note: Mathlib's Banach open mapping theorem over a nontrivially normed field (Mathlib/Analysis/Normed/Operator/Banach.lean:229); Tau Ceti also has Henkel's version over Tate rings (TauCeti.Huber.IsTateRing.isOpenMap).

items.name: The p-finite case of the sheaf theorem
items.statement: Let K have characteristic p and (R, R⁺) be p-finite, the completed perfection of the reduced tft (S, S⁺). (i) X = Spa(R, R⁺) → Y = Spa(S, S⁺) is a homeomorphism identifying rational subsets. (ii) For rational U ⊂ X corresponding to V ⊂ Y, (𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)) is the completed perfection of (𝒪_Y(V), 𝒪_Y⁺(V)). (iii) For every rational cover, 0 → 𝒪_X(X)°a → ∏ 𝒪_X(U_i)°a → ⋯ is exact; so 𝒪_X is a sheaf and H^i(X, 𝒪_X°a) = 0 for i > 0 (Remark 6.12: equivalently H^i(X, 𝒪_X⁺) is killed by m).

items.name: Perfectoid affinoids in characteristic p are completed limits of p-finite ones
items.statement: Let K have characteristic p. (i) A perfectoid affinoid (R, R⁺) with R⁺ a K°-algebra is the completion of a filtered direct limit of p-finite (R_i, R_i⁺). (ii) Then Spa(R, R⁺) ≅ lim Spa(R_i, R_i⁺), and every rational U ⊂ X is the preimage of a rational U_i ⊂ X_i. (iii) (𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)) is the completion of lim_j (𝒪_{X_j}(U_j), 𝒪⁺_{X_j}(U_j)). (iv) If U_i ⊂ X_i is quasicompact open and contains the image of X, the image of some X_j lies in U_i.
items.locator: §6, Lemma 6.13 and proof, p. 293 (Tate [33, Theorem 5.2] for S_I⁺)
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/completed-direct-limits-of-p-finite-affinoids. The proof of (iv) says "zero" for "empty" (source issue E4, recorded in the atlas as PerfectoidSpaces/E14).

items.name: The sheaf theorem and almost acyclicity for perfectoid affinoids
items.statement: For every perfectoid affinoid (R, R⁺) over K of any characteristic and every cover of X = Spa(R, R⁺) by finitely many rational subsets, 0 → 𝒪_X(X)°a → ∏ 𝒪_X(U_i)°a → ∏ 𝒪_X(U_i ∩ U_j)°a → ⋯ is exact. Hence 𝒪_X (and 𝒪_{X♭}) is a sheaf, H^i(X, 𝒪_X°a) = 0 and H^i(X, 𝒪_X⁺) is m-torsion for i > 0 (Theorem 6.3(iii)–(iv), Theorem 1.8(iii)–(iv)).
items.locator: §6, Proposition 6.14 and proof, pp. 293–294; Theorem 6.3(iii)–(iv), p. 284
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/sheaf-theorem-and-almost-acyclicity. P2 also plans the acyclic-basis comparison from Čech to sheaf cohomology, which the paper does not write out.

items.name: Perfectoid spaces
items.statement: The affinoid adic space Spa(R, R⁺) of a perfectoid affinoid K-algebra is an affinoid perfectoid space. A perfectoid space is an adic space over K locally isomorphic to an affinoid perfectoid space; morphisms are morphisms of adic spaces.
items.locator: §6, the paragraph before Definition 6.15 and Definition 6.15, p. 294
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/perfectoid-spaces-and-glued-tilting.

items.name: Tilting of perfectoid spaces
items.statement: A perfectoid space X♭ over K♭ is a tilt of X over K if Hom(Spa(R♭, R♭⁺), X♭) = Hom(Spa(R, R⁺), X) functorially in perfectoid affinoid (R, R⁺) (Definition 6.16). Every perfectoid space X has a tilt, unique up to unique isomorphism; this gives an equivalence between perfectoid spaces over K and over K♭ (Theorem 1.9); |X| = |X♭|; X is affinoid perfectoid iff X♭ is; and for every affinoid perfectoid U ⊂ X, (𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)) is perfectoid affinoid with tilt (𝒪_{X♭}(U♭), 𝒪⁺_{X♭}(U♭)).
items.locator: §6, Definition 6.16, Proposition 6.17 and proof, pp. 294–295; §1, Theorem 1.9, p. 248

items.name: Fibre products of perfectoid spaces
items.statement: For perfectoid spaces X → Y ← Z over K the fibre product X ×_Y Z exists in adic spaces over K and is perfectoid; for X = Spa(A, A⁺), Y = Spa(B, B⁺), Z = Spa(C, C⁺) it is Spa(D, D⁺) with D the completion of A ⊗_B C and D⁺ the completion of the integral closure of the image of A⁺ ⊗_{B⁺} C⁺, and the completed almost tensor product A°a ⊗̂_{B°a} C°a is a perfectoid K°a-algebra.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P2/fibre-products-of-perfectoid-spaces; A0 supplies completed tensor products.

items.name: Finite étale and étale morphisms of adic spaces
items.statement: Over an arbitrary nonarchimedean field k: (i) (R, R⁺) → (S, S⁺) is finite étale if S is a finite étale R-algebra with the induced topology and S⁺ is the integral closure of R⁺ in S; (ii) f : X → Y is finite étale if Y has a cover by open affinoids V with f^{-1}(V) affinoid and (𝒪_Y(V), 𝒪_Y⁺(V)) → (𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)) finite étale; (iii) f is étale if every x has neighbourhoods U, V with f|_U = p ∘ j, j an open embedding and p finite étale. For locally noetherian adic spaces (locally Spa of a strongly noetherian Tate algebra; noetherian if also qcqs) these agree with Huber's notions ([22, Example 1.6.6(ii), Lemma 2.2.8]).
items.locator: §7, the opening paragraph and Definition 7.1, pp. 295–296
items.note: A1 defines finite étale and étale adic morphisms by these local descriptions and compares with Huber's definitions; node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change.

items.name: Strongly finite étale and strongly étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces
items.statement: (i) A morphism of perfectoid affinoid K-algebras is strongly finite étale if it is finite étale and S°a is finite étale over R°a. (ii), (iii) Strongly finite étale and strongly étale morphisms of perfectoid spaces are defined locally as in Definition 7.1. f is strongly (finite) étale iff its tilt f♭ is (Proposition 6.17, Theorem 5.25); in characteristic p every (finite) étale morphism is strongly (finite) étale.
items.locator: §7, Definition 7.2 and the paragraph after it, p. 296

items.name: Base change of (strongly) (finite) étale morphisms
items.statement: (i) If f : X → Y is strongly finite étale (resp. strongly étale) and g : Z → Y is any morphism of perfectoid spaces, X ×_Y Z → Z is strongly finite étale (resp. strongly étale), and |X ×_Y Z| → |X| ×_{|Y|} |Z| is surjective. (ii) For affinoids with (A, A⁺) strongly finite étale over (B, B⁺), X ×_Y Z = Spa(D, D⁺) with D = A ⊗_B C and D⁺ the integral closure of C⁺ in D. (iii), (iv) In characteristic p the same holds for a (finite) étale morphism of adic spaces X → Y and a perfectoid Z → Y: the fibre product exists in adic spaces, is perfectoid, and the projection is (finite) étale.
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-etale-morphisms-and-base-change. The surjectivity is printed as |X ×_Z Y| → |X| ×_{|Z|} |Y| (source issue E2, recorded in the atlas as PerfectoidSpaces/E22 and AdicEtaleGeometry/E3).

items.name: Finite étale algebras over a henselian pair and its completion
items.statement: For a flat K°-algebra A henselian along (ϖ), finite étale A[ϖ^{-1}]-algebras and finite étale Â[ϖ^{-1}]-algebras are equivalent (Â the ϖ-adic completion). ϖ-adically complete algebras are henselian along (ϖ), and filtered colimits of algebras henselian along (ϖ) are henselian along (ϖ).
items.locator: §7, Proposition 7.4 and the sentence after it, pp. 297–298 (Gabber–Ramero [15, Proposition 5.4.53])
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/henselian-finite-etale-approximation (the decomposition moved this input from P5 to P3). Mathlib's HenselianRing is the henselian-pair notion.

items.name: Finite étale algebras and completed direct limits
items.statement: (i) If A_i is a filtered system of complete flat K°-algebras and A the completion of lim A_i, then A[ϖ^{-1}]_fét ≅ 2-lim (A_i[ϖ^{-1}])_fét; in particular R_fét ≅ 2-lim (R_i)_fét for a completed direct limit R of perfectoid K-algebras R_i. (ii) If K has characteristic p and (R, R⁺) is p-finite, the completed perfection of (S, S⁺), then R_fét ≅ S_fét.

items.name: Strongly finite étale maps are affinoid over affinoid perfectoids
items.statement: If f : X → Y is strongly finite étale, then for every open affinoid perfectoid V ⊂ Y the preimage U is affinoid perfectoid and (𝒪_Y(V), 𝒪_Y⁺(V)) → (𝒪_X(U), 𝒪_X⁺(U)) is strongly finite étale. Hence, in characteristic p, finite étale covers of Spa(R, R⁺) are the finite étale covers of R.
items.locator: §7, Proposition 7.6, proof and the sentence after it, pp. 298–299
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/strongly-finite-etale-maps-are-affinoid-over-affinoids; reduces to Huber [22, Example 1.6.6(ii)].

items.name: Étale maps in characteristic p come from noetherian adic spaces
items.statement: If K has characteristic p and f : X → Y is an étale map of perfectoid spaces, then every x ∈ X has affinoid perfectoid neighbourhoods x ∈ U ⊂ X, f(U) ⊂ V ⊂ Y and an étale morphism of affinoid noetherian adic spaces U_0 → V_0 over K with U = U_0 ×_{V_0} V.

items.name: Strongly étale maps are open and stable under composition
items.statement: Strongly étale maps of perfectoid spaces are open, and composites of strongly (finite) étale maps are strongly (finite) étale.

items.name: The almost purity theorem
items.statement: Let (R, R⁺) be perfectoid affinoid, X = Spa(R, R⁺). (i) For every open affinoid perfectoid U ⊂ X, global sections give a fully faithful functor from strongly finite étale covers of U to finite étale 𝒪_X(U)-algebras. (ii) This functor is an equivalence. (iii) For every finite étale S/R, S is perfectoid and S°a is finite étale over R°a, and S°a is a uniformly almost finitely generated R°a-module (Theorem 1.10). Consequently every (finite) étale morphism of perfectoid spaces is strongly (finite) étale.
items.locator: §7, Theorem 7.9, proof and the sentence after it, pp. 299–301; §1, Theorem 1.10, p. 248
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/almost-purity-theorem. The proof localises using Lemma 7.5(i), untilts over completed residue fields with Theorem 3.7, and glues with the sheaf property.

items.name: Pulling back étale maps of adic spaces in characteristic 0
items.statement: Lemma 7.3(iii)–(iv) hold also when K has characteristic 0: for a (finite) étale morphism of adic spaces X → Y and a perfectoid space Z → Y, X ×_Y Z exists, is perfectoid, and X ×_Y Z → Z is (finite) étale.

items.name: The étale site of a perfectoid space
items.statement: For a perfectoid space X, X_ét is the category of perfectoid spaces étale over X with coverings the topological coverings; X~_ét is its topos. A morphism of perfectoid spaces X → Y, and a morphism from a perfectoid space to a locally noetherian adic space, induce morphisms of sites X_ét → Y_ét.
items.locator: §7, Definition 7.11 and the paragraph after it, p. 301

items.name: Tilting identifies étale sites
items.statement: For a perfectoid space X over K with tilt X♭, tilting induces an isomorphism of sites X_ét ≅ X♭_ét, functorial in X (Theorem 1.12).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P3/etale-site-tilting-and-etale-almost-acyclicity.

items.name: Almost acyclicity of 𝒪° on the étale site
items.statement: For a perfectoid space X, U ↦ 𝒪_U(U) is a sheaf 𝒪_X on X_ét, and H^i(X_ét, 𝒪_X°a) = 0 for i > 0 if X is affinoid perfectoid.

items.name: X ∼ lim X_i for a perfectoid space over noetherian adic spaces
items.statement: For a perfectoid space X, a filtered inverse system (X_i) of noetherian adic spaces over K and compatible maps X → X_i, write X ∼ lim X_i if |X| → lim |X_i| is a homeomorphism and, for every x ∈ X with images x_i, lim_i k(x_i) → k(x) has dense image. Then |X| is spectral, hence qcqs (Remark 7.15).
items.note: Node PerfectoidSpaces:P7/tilde-limits-and-etale-topos-comparison; H0 insists that a tilde-limit is not a categorical inverse limit.

items.name: Tilde-limits are stable under étale base change
items.statement: In the situation of Definition 7.14, if Y → X_i is an étale morphism of noetherian adic spaces, then Y ×_{X_i} X ∼ lim_{j≥i} Y ×_{X_i} X_j. Moreover bijectivity of |X| → lim |X_i| together with the residue-field condition already implies X ∼ lim X_i.
items.locator: §7, Proposition 7.16 and proof, p. 302 (as Huber [22, Remark 2.4.3])

items.name: The étale topos of a tilde-limit
items.statement: In the situation of Definition 7.14, X~_ét is a projective limit of the fibred topos (X~_{i,ét})_i (SGA 4 VI §8).
items.locator: §7, Theorem 7.17 and proof, p. 302 (as Huber [22, Proposition 2.4.4], with Lemma 7.5)

items.name: Cohomology of a tilde-limit
items.statement: In the situation of Definition 7.14, for a sheaf of abelian groups F_i on X_{i,ét} with pullbacks F_j (j ≥ i) and F on X_ét, lim_j H^n(X_{j,ét}, F_j) → H^n(X_ét, F) is bijective for all n ≥ 0.

items.name: Purely inseparable towers do not change the étale topos
items.statement: If in Definition 7.14 all transition maps X_j → X_i induce purely inseparable extensions of completed residue fields and homeomorphisms |X_j| → |X_i|, then X~_ét is equivalent to X~_{i,ét} for every i.
items.locator: §7, Corollary 7.19 and proof, p. 303 (Huber [22], remark after Proposition 2.3.7)

items.name: Toric varieties
items.statement: A toric variety over a field k is a normal separated scheme X of finite type over k with an action of a split torus T ≅ 𝔾_m^r and a point x ∈ X(k) with trivial stabiliser in T whose orbit T ≅ Tx = U ⊂ X is open and dense.
items.note: The Tau Ceti roadmap Analytic toric geometry plans toric schemes only over ℂ (Layer 0: affine toric scheme Spec ℂ[S_σ], link to a ToricVariety instance), and none is built. Routed to the nonarchimedean toric Part II. (The paper uses k both for the field and the rank of T; r is used here.)

items.name: Strongly convex rational polyhedral cones and fans
items.statement: Let N be a free abelian group of finite rank. (i) A strongly convex polyhedral cone is σ = ℝ_{≥0}x_1 + ⋯ + ℝ_{≥0}x_n ⊂ N ⊗ ℝ with x_i ∈ N, containing no line through the origin. (ii) A fan Σ is a nonempty finite collection of such cones, closed under faces, such that the intersection of two cones of Σ is a face of each.
items.note: Tau Ceti's IsToricCone (lattice-rational and salient Mathlib pointed cone; TauCeti/Geometry/Toric/Algebraic/Cone.lean:124) and Fan (finite, closed under faces, pairwise intersections faces; Fan/Basic.lean:81); the dual cone is Mathlib's PointedCone.dual.

items.name: The toric variety X_Σ of a fan
items.statement: With M = Hom(N, ℤ), a cone σ gives σ^∨ ⊂ M ⊗ ℝ and U_σ = Spec k[σ^∨ ∩ M], with χ^u the function of u ∈ σ^∨ ∩ M. For a face τ of σ, σ^∨ ⊂ τ^∨ gives an open immersion U_τ → U_σ; these glue to X_Σ. T = U_{0} = Spec k[M] acts with open dense orbit, and 1 ∈ T gives the base point, making X_Σ a toric variety.
items.note: Analytic toric geometry Layer 0 plans the dual semigroup, affine toric schemes over ℂ and their gluing, all absent in Tau Ceti. Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry C0 (ShimuraCompactifications:C0) plans affine toric charts over the base rings of integral models and torus embeddings relative to a torus torsor (packet nodes C0/relative-torus-embedding, C0/relative-face-open), for the arithmetic fans of toroidal compactifications. The finite-fan scheme X_Σ over an arbitrary field, and over k° as used in the rest of §8, is not planned; it goes to the nonarchimedean toric Part II, which imports C0's charts.

items.name: Classification of toric varieties by fans
items.statement: Every toric variety over k is canonically isomorphic to X_Σ for a unique fan Σ in X_*(T) ⊗ ℝ.
items.note: Recalled without proof (it needs Sumihiro's theorem). Not planned; routed to the toric Part II. Theorem 9.6 is stated for a toric variety but the proof works with X_Σ.

items.name: Torus-invariant divisors and their sections
items.statement: Let τ_i ∈ Σ be the one-dimensional cones with primitive generators v_i ∈ τ_i ∩ N. Each τ_i gives U_{τ_i} ≅ 𝔸¹ × 𝔾_m^{r−1} and a T-invariant Weil divisor D_i, the closure of {0} × 𝔾_m^{r−1}. T-Weil divisors are the elements of ⊕ ℤ D_i; every Weil divisor is equivalent to one; and for D = Σ a_i D_i, H⁰(X_Σ, 𝒪(D)) = ⊕_{u ∈ M, ⟨u, v_i⟩ ≥ −a_i} k χ^u.
items.note: Primitive ray generators exist in Tau Ceti (TauCeti/Geometry/Toric/Algebraic/Ray/Primitive.lean); divisors and their sections are not planned over a field (Analytic toric geometry Layer 4 plans invariant analytic hypersurfaces over ℂ). Routed to the toric Part II.

items.name: The adic toric space X_Σ^ad of a fan
items.statement: For k complete nonarchimedean, X_Σ^ad is the adic space of finite type over k glued from U_σ^ad = Spa(k⟨σ^∨ ∩ M⟩, k°⟨σ^∨ ∩ M⟩). It is the generic fibre of the formal completion of the toric k°-scheme X_{Σ,k°} along its special fibre (an admissible formal scheme); in general it differs from the analytification (X_Σ)^ad (for affine space it is the closed unit ball), and it equals it when X_Σ is proper. Multiplication by p on M induces φ : X_Σ^ad → X_Σ^ad.
