items.note: Needs the formal generic fibre of AdicSpacesPartII:R2 and the analytification of R1. Routed to the toric Part II.

items.name: The perfectoid toric space X_Σ^perf and its line bundles
items.statement: For a perfectoid field K, X_Σ^perf is the perfectoid space glued from U_σ^perf = Spa(K⟨(σ^∨ ∩ M)[p^{-1}]⟩, K°⟨(σ^∨ ∩ M)[p^{-1}]⟩). On it there is a sheaf 𝒪(D) for every D ∈ ⊕ ℤ[p^{-1}] D_i, and H⁰(X_Σ^perf, 𝒪(D)) is the Banach K-space with orthonormal basis χ^u, u ∈ M[p^{-1}] with ⟨u, v_i⟩ ≥ −a_i.
items.note: The affine pieces are perfectoid by the argument of Proposition 5.20; P7 lists compatible-root discs and tori only as tests. Routed to the toric Part II.

items.name: The perfectoid toric space tilts to the perfectoid toric space
items.statement: For a perfectoid field K with tilt K♭, the perfectoid space X^perf_{Σ,K} tilts to X^perf_{Σ,K♭} (checked on affinoid pieces as in Proposition 5.20).
items.note: Routed to the toric Part II.

items.name: The perfectoid toric space as a tilde-limit
items.statement: X^perf_{Σ,K} ∼ lim_φ X^ad_{Σ,K} in the sense of Definition 7.14 (checked on affinoid pieces).
items.note: Uses P7 (tilde-limits). Routed to the toric Part II.

items.name: The tilted toric space as an inverse limit of topological spaces
items.statement: There is a homeomorphism |X^ad_{Σ,K♭}| ≅ lim_φ |X^ad_{Σ,K}|; it defines the projection π : X^ad_{Σ,K♭} → X^ad_{Σ,K} on topological spaces, given on coordinates by π(x_0 : ⋯ : x_n) = (x_0♯ : ⋯ : x_n♯) for ℙⁿ.
items.locator: §8, Theorem 8.5(iii), proof and the sentence after it, p. 305; §1, pp. 249–250
items.note: From (i), (ii), Theorem 7.17, Corollary 7.19 and |X| = |X♭|; X^ad_{Σ,K♭} is not perfectoid, but its φ-tower is and φ is purely inseparable. Routed to the toric Part II.

items.name: Étale topoi of the tilted toric space
items.statement: There is an equivalence of étale topoi (X^ad_{Σ,K♭})~_ét ≅ lim_φ (X^ad_{Σ,K})~_ét (inverse limit of a fibred topos), giving π on étale topoi. For Σ the fan of ℙⁿ this is Theorem 1.13: (ℙ^{n,ad}_{K♭})~_ét ≅ lim_φ (ℙ^{n,ad}_K)~_ét with φ(x_0 : ⋯ : x_n) = (x_0^p : ⋯ : x_n^p); the same holds for proper toric varieties and hence for rigid-analytic varieties.
items.locator: §8, Theorem 8.5(iv) and proof, p. 305; §1, Theorem 1.13, p. 249
items.note: Routed to the toric Part II.

items.name: Compatibility of π with open subsets
items.statement: For every open U ⊂ X^ad_{Σ,K} with preimage V ⊂ X^ad_{Σ,K♭} there is a morphism of étale topoi V~_ét → U~_ét compatible with π : (X^ad_{Σ,K♭})~_ét → (X^ad_{Σ,K})~_ét and the inclusions.
items.note: Routed to the toric Part II.

items.name: π induces isomorphisms on torsion étale cohomology of proper smooth toric varieties
items.statement: Let X_Σ be a proper smooth toric variety, ℓ ≠ p a prime and K (hence K♭) algebraically closed. For all i, π induces H^i(X^ad_{Σ,K,ét}, ℤ/ℓ^mℤ) ≅ H^i(X^ad_{Σ,K♭,ét}, ℤ/ℓ^mℤ). (Proof: by (iv) it suffices that φ acts isomorphically on ℤ/ℓ^m-cohomology; by proper base change this is checked on X_{Σ,κ} over the residue field κ, where φ is purely inseparable and induces an equivalence of étale topoi.)
items.note: Imports proper base change (item 131) and topological invariance of the étale site (item 132). Routed to the toric Part II.

items.name: Proper base change for a proper smooth model
items.statement: For a proper smooth scheme over K° (here the toric scheme X_{Σ,K°}) and ℓ ≠ p, the ℤ/ℓ^m-cohomology of the geometric generic fibre is identified with that of the special fibre X_{Σ,κ}, compatibly with φ.
items.note: SF.2 plans proper and smooth base change for étale cohomology of schemes; with Theorem 9.7 this transfers to the adic spaces.

items.name: Purely inseparable maps induce equivalences of étale topoi
items.statement: A finite surjective purely inseparable (radicial) morphism, such as the Frobenius-type map φ on X_{Σ,κ} in characteristic p or on adic spaces over K♭, induces an equivalence of étale topoi.
items.locator: §1, p. 250; §8, proof of Proposition 8.6, p. 306; §7, Corollary 7.19, p. 303
items.note: Topological invariance of the étale site (SGA 4 VIII 1.1) is part of SF.2's étale-site comparisons for schemes; the adic version is Corollary 7.19 (P7).

items.name: The approximation lemma for the graded perfectoid ring of a toric divisor
items.statement: For a T-Weil divisor D on X_{Σ,K}, let R be the completion (for the obvious K°-submodule) of the Banach direct sum ⊕_{j ∈ ℤ[p^{-1}]} H⁰(X^perf_{Σ,K}, 𝒪(jD)) = ⊕_j ⊕_{u ∈ M[p^{-1}], ⟨u,v_i⟩ ≥ −j a_i} K χ^u. Then R is a perfectoid K-algebra whose tilt is the same construction over K♭, and the analogue of Lemma 6.5 holds for R with the same proof: every homogeneous f can be approximated by g♯ with g homogeneous of the same degree over K♭.
items.note: Asserted with "the same proof" as Proposition 5.20 and Lemma 6.5. Routed to the toric Part II (route 5). It identifies R_D and its tilt with the Banach-completed perfected monoid algebra of the rational cone C_D = {(u, j) : ⟨u, v_i⟩ ≥ −j a_i for all i}, graded by j, and imports the approximation induction from PerfectoidSpaces P2 (PerfectoidSpaces:P2/approximation-lemma, stated there for the perfectoid polydisc), through a request that P2 state it for such cone algebras; the induction is not planned twice (RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12/6).

items.name: Approximating a hypersurface by a tilted hypersurface
items.statement: Let X_{Σ,K} be proper smooth, Y ⊂ X_{Σ,K} a hypersurface and Ỹ ⊂ X^ad_{Σ,K} a small open neighbourhood of Y. Then there is a hypersurface Z ⊂ X_{Σ,K♭} with Z^ad ⊂ π^{-1}(Ỹ), and Z can be chosen defined over any given dense subfield of K♭. (Lemma 1.16 is the case of ℙⁿ.) Proof: Y = {f = 0}, f ∈ H⁰(X_{Σ,K}, 𝒪(D)); Ỹ = {|f(x)| ≤ ε} using the tautological integral model of X_{Σ,K} and 𝒪(D) over K°; the graded approximation lemma gives g ∈ H⁰(X^perf_{Σ,K♭}, 𝒪(D)) with π^{-1}(Ỹ) = {|g(x)| ≤ ε}; perturb g to have coefficients in the dense subfield; a large p-power of g is a section h of 𝒪(p^N D) on X_{Σ,K♭}, and Z = {h = 0} ⊂ π^{-1}(Ỹ).
items.locator: §8, Proposition 8.7 and proof, pp. 306–307; §1, Lemma 1.16, p. 251
items.note: The proof calls h a "regular function" (source issue E11). Routed to the toric Part II; it is the endpoint named in the BKV brief for that Part II.

items.name: Approximating a complete intersection
items.statement: Let X_{Σ,K} be projective and smooth, Y ⊂ X_{Σ,K} a set-theoretic complete intersection (Y = Y_1 ∩ ⋯ ∩ Y_c set-theoretically, hypersurfaces Y_i, c = codim Y) and Ỹ a small open neighbourhood of Y. Then there is a closed subvariety Z ⊂ X_{Σ,K♭} with Z^ad ⊂ π^{-1}(Ỹ) and dim Z = dim Y, definable over any given dense subfield of K♭. (Nonemptiness: with an ample line bundle the degree of a complete intersection is combinatorial, and Y has positive degree; cut down by further hypersurfaces if the dimension is too large.)
items.note: The degree argument needs intersection theory with refined intersections (item 151 uses the same ingredients); routed to the toric Part II.

items.name: The tame character t_ℓ of inertia
items.statement: For a local field k of residue characteristic p with residue field of order q, the maximal pro-ℓ quotient of the inertia group I_k ⊂ G_k = Gal(k̄/k) is t_ℓ : I_k → ℤ_ℓ(1), the inverse limit of t_{ℓ,n} : I_k → μ_{ℓ^n}, σ(ϖ^{1/ℓ^n}) = t_{ℓ,n}(σ) ϖ^{1/ℓ^n} for a compatible system of ℓ^n-th roots of a uniformiser ϖ.
items.note: Local fields and ramification Layer 4 plans I_K/P_K ≅ Ẑ^{(p′)}(1) with its specialisation at one prime ℓ ≠ p; LPV.1 plans t_ℓ for the monodromy operator.

items.name: Grothendieck's quasi-unipotence theorem and the monodromy operator
items.statement: For a finite-dimensional Q̄_ℓ-representation ρ : G_k → GL(V) there is an open subgroup I_1 ⊂ I_k acting unipotently, and then a unique nilpotent N : V → V(−1) with ρ(σ) = exp(N t_ℓ(σ)) for all σ ∈ I_1. After fixing ℚ_ℓ(1) ≅ ℚ_ℓ, N is a nilpotent endomorphism, determined up to a scalar.
items.locator: §9, Proposition 9.1 and the paragraph after it, pp. 307–308
items.note: Printed as exp(N t_ℓ(g)) (source issue E1). LPV.1 plans N, exp(t_ℓ(σ)N) = ρ(σ) and quasi-unipotence in the geometric setting; R01.2 plans quasi-unipotence and Weil–Deligne representations for arithmetic representations.

items.name: The Frobenius–monodromy relation
items.statement: For every geometric Frobenius Φ ∈ G_k, N Φ = q Φ N (from the uniqueness of N).
items.note: R01.2 plans the relation (in the arithmetic-Frobenius normalisation r(F)Nr(F)^{-1} = qN, warning against copying the geometric formula); DWP.5 includes the Frobenius–N relation.

items.name: The monodromy filtration
items.statement: For a nilpotent endomorphism N of a finite-dimensional vector space V over any field there is a unique separated exhaustive increasing filtration Fil_i^N V (i ∈ ℤ) with N(Fil_i^N V) ⊂ Fil_{i−2}^N V and N^i : gr_i^N V ≅ gr_{−i}^N V for i ≥ 0; explicitly Fil_i^N V = Σ_{i_1 − i_2 = i} ker N^{i_1+1} ∩ im N^{i_2}.
items.locator: §9, Definition/Proposition 9.2 and the formula after it, pp. 307–308
items.note: LPV.1 plans the uniquely characterised centred monodromy filtration (linear algebra, independent of weights).

items.name: The weight-monodromy conjecture for a proper smooth variety
items.statement: Conjecture 9.3 (Deligne): for a proper smooth variety X over a local field k and V = H^i(X_k̄, Q̄_ℓ) satisfies weight–monodromy of weight i (item 154): for all j ∈ ℤ and every geometric Frobenius Φ ∈ G_k, all eigenvalues of Φ on gr_j^N V are Weil numbers of weight i + j, i.e. algebraic numbers α with |α| = q^{(i+j)/2} for all complex absolute values. "WMC holds for X" means this statement for all i. (Conjecture 1.14; the paper records its L-function interpretation: at primes of bad reduction the local factor det(1 − q^{−s}Φ | H^i(X)^{I_k})^{-1} would have no poles with real part > i/2.)
items.locator: §9, Conjecture 9.3 and the paragraph after it, p. 308; §1, Conjecture 1.14, p. 250
items.note: Split by RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12/7. The definitional half, weight–monodromy purity of a Weil–Deligne or local Galois representation, is item 154, routed to DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.5 (route 7). This item is the conjecture for a proper smooth variety, which uses it. No stage owns the mixed-characteristic conjecture: DWP.5 says explicitly that its local weight theory is not the mixed-characteristic conjecture, and R34.6 that the general conjecture is not assumed. Routed to the weight-monodromy Part II (route 6).

items.name: Weight-monodromy may be checked after finite or totally ramified pro-p base change
items.statement: To prove the weight-monodromy conjecture one may replace k by a finite extension. It may also be checked after restricting to G_K for K the completion of k(ϖ^{1/p^∞}), ϖ a uniformiser: the extension is totally ramified, so geometric Frobenii of G_K still give the weight decomposition, and it is pro-p, so the pro-ℓ inertia (hence N) is still seen.
items.locator: §9, the sentence after Conjecture 9.3, p. 308, and the start of the proof of Theorem 9.6, p. 309
items.note: The second reduction is only in the published version (arXiv v1 omits it). Routed to the weight-monodromy Part II.

items.name: Deligne's weight-monodromy theorem in equal characteristic
items.statement: Let C be a curve over 𝔽_q, x ∈ C(𝔽_q), and k the local field of C at x. For a proper smooth scheme X over C ∖ {x}, the weight-monodromy conjecture holds for X_k = X ×_{C∖{x}} Spec k. (Proof sketch: after a finite cover, I_k acts unipotently on V = H^i(X_k̄, Q̄_ℓ); R^i f_* Q̄_ℓ is pure of weight i by the Weil conjectures; semicontinuity of weights gives weights ≤ i on V^{I_k}, likewise for tensor powers of V and V^∨; conclude by Lemma 9.5.)
items.locator: §9, Theorem 9.4 and the summary of its proof, pp. 308–309 (Deligne [10])
items.note: DWP.5 plans the local weight theorem for a punctually pure lisse sheaf on an open curve (weights of monodromy graded pieces, boundary invariants, tensor and dual compatibility); purity of R^i f_* for proper smooth f is DWP.4/DWP.7. The general equal-characteristic case (Terasoma, Ito) is not needed here.

items.name: The linear-algebra criterion for weight-monodromy
items.statement: Let V be an ℓ-adic representation of G_k on which I_k acts unipotently, and i an integer. Then gr_j^N V is pure of weight i + j for all j ∈ ℤ if and only if for all j ≥ 0 all weights on (V^{⊗j})^{I_k} are at most ij and all weights on ((V^∨)^{⊗j})^{I_k} are at most −ij.
items.note: The printed statement does not introduce i (source issue E8). DWP.5 names Weil II 1.8.4 as a source.

items.name: Weight-monodromy for complete intersections in toric varieties
items.statement: Let k be a local field of characteristic 0 and Y a geometrically connected proper smooth variety over k that is a set-theoretic complete intersection in a projective smooth toric variety X_Σ. Then the weight-monodromy conjecture holds for Y (Theorem 1.15; already new for smooth hypersurfaces in ℙⁿ).
items.locator: §9, Theorem 9.6 and proof, pp. 309–311; §1, Theorem 1.15 and the sketch after it, p. 251
items.note: The main theorem. Routed to the weight-monodromy Part II, importing the toric approximation (Corollary 8.8, Proposition 8.6) from the toric Part II.

items.name: Identifying G_K with the Galois group of a Laurent-series field, compatibly with weights and N
items.statement: For K the completion of k(ϖ^{1/p^∞}), K♭ is the completed perfection of k′ = 𝔽_q((t)) with t = ϖ♭, which gives G_K ≅ G_{K♭} ≅ G_{k′}; the notions of weights (geometric Frobenii) and of the monodromy operator N are compatible with this isomorphism.
items.locator: §9, proof of Theorem 9.6, first paragraph, p. 309
items.note: Combines Theorem 1.3 with the invariance of absolute Galois groups under completion and perfection (item 2, planned by PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger) and the compatibility of inertia, Frobenius and t_ℓ, which the paper asserts. Routed to the weight-monodromy Part II.

items.name: Huber's theorem: a small neighbourhood has the same cohomology
items.statement: For a closed subvariety Y ⊂ X_Σ over K (here Y^ad_K ⊂ X^ad_{Σ,K}) there is an open neighbourhood Ỹ of Y^ad_K such that Ỹ_{ℂ_p} and Y^ad_{ℂ_p} have the same ℤ/ℓℤ-cohomology, hence (by induction) the same ℤ/ℓ^mℤ-cohomology for all m ≥ 1.
items.locator: §9, proof of Theorem 9.6, second paragraph, p. 309 (Huber [21, Theorem 3.6(a)])
items.note: Cited from Huber, A finiteness result for direct image sheaves on the étale site of rigid analytic varieties (J. Algebraic Geom. 7 (1998)); no stage plans it (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H5 plans other Huber comparison and continuity results). Routed to the weight-monodromy Part II; Huber 1998 is listed as a prerequisite.

items.name: Huber's comparison of algebraic and adic étale cohomology
items.statement: For an algebraic variety X over an algebraically closed nonarchimedean field k with adic space X^ad, H^i(X_ét, ℤ/ℓ^mℤ) ≅ H^i(X^ad_ét, ℤ/ℓ^mℤ).
items.note: H5 plans the cases of Huber's Theorems 3.7.2 and 3.8.1 used in ECD §27; the use here (ℓ ≠ p, proper smooth Y and the ambient toric variety) is within Huber's statement, and the WMC Part II must check that H5 exports it in this generality.

items.name: De Jong's alterations
items.statement: A variety Z over a field has a projective smooth alteration Z′ → Z (proper, surjective, generically finite, Z′ smooth projective); used for a geometrically irreducible Z defined over a global function field.
items.note: L5 plans de Jong's Theorem 4.1 (alteration to a smooth situation in the field case).

items.name: The Galois-equivariant comparison map from Y to the tilted approximation
items.statement: With Z ⊂ X_{Σ,K♭} from Corollary 8.8 (defined over a global field, geometrically irreducible) and Z′ a projective smooth alteration, the commutative diagram of étale topoi (X^ad_{Σ,ℂ_p♭})~ → (X^ad_{Σ,ℂ_p})~, (π^{-1}(Ỹ)_{ℂ_p♭})~ → (Ỹ_{ℂ_p})~, (Z′^ad_{ℂ_p♭})~ → (π^{-1}(Ỹ)_{ℂ_p♭})~, (Y^ad_{ℂ_p})~ → (Ỹ_{ℂ_p})~ carries a canonical action of G = G_K = G_{K♭} making all maps equivariant, and with Theorem 9.7 gives a G-equivariant map f* : H^i(Y_{ℂ_p,ét}, ℤ/ℓ^m) = H^i(Ỹ_{ℂ_p,ét}, ℤ/ℓ^m) → H^i(Z′_{ℂ_p♭,ét}, ℤ/ℓ^m), compatible with cup products; passing to the limit and tensoring, H^i(Y_{ℂ_p,ét}, Q̄_ℓ) → H^i(Z′_{ℂ_p♭,ét}, Q̄_ℓ).
items.note: Cup-product compatibility is Lemma 9.8 plus the remark that the identification H^i(Y) = H^i(Ỹ) is an isomorphism. Routed to the weight-monodromy Part II.

items.name: Pullback along a morphism of sites respects cup products
items.statement: For a morphism of sites f : T_1 → T_2, a ring A and α ∈ H^i(T_2, A), β ∈ H^j(T_2, A): (f*α) ∪ (f*β) = f*(α ∪ β) in H^{i+j}(T_1, A) (cup product as composition A → A[i] → A[i + j] in the derived category, preserved by the functor f*).
items.note: Only in the published version. No stage defines cup products on the cohomology of a general site (the Tau Ceti profinite-cohomology cup products are group cohomology). Routed to the weight-monodromy Part II; it may be supplied by whichever roadmap owns sheaf cohomology on sites.

items.name: The comparison map is an isomorphism in top degree
items.statement: For i = 2 dim Y, H^{2dim Y}(Y_{ℂ_p,ét}, Q̄_ℓ) → H^{2dim Y}(Z′_{ℂ_p♭,ét}, Q̄_ℓ) is an isomorphism. (Proof: in the diagram with the ambient toric variety, the top row is an isomorphism by Proposition 8.6; if the map were not an isomorphism it would be zero, as H^{2dim Y}(Y) is one-dimensional, so restriction from X_{Σ,ℂ_p♭} to Z′ would vanish in degree 2 dim Y; but the (dim Y)-th power of the first Chern class of an ample line bundle on X_{Σ,ℂ_p♭} has nonzero image in H^{2dim Y}(Z′).)
items.locator: §9, Lemma 9.9 and proof, pp. 310–311 (Lemma 9.8 in arXiv v1)
items.note: Uses Chern classes and their nonvanishing on a variety of the right dimension (item 153). Routed to the weight-monodromy Part II.

items.name: H^i(Y) is a Galois-stable direct summand of H^i(Z′)
items.statement: By Poincaré duality (and the cup-product compatibility and the top-degree isomorphism), H^i(Y_{ℂ_p,ét}, Q̄_ℓ) is a direct summand of H^i(Z′_{ℂ_p♭,ét}, Q̄_ℓ) as a G-representation; since H^i(Z′) satisfies weight-monodromy by Deligne's theorem (Z′ comes from a variety over a global function field), so does its direct summand, proving Theorem 9.6.
items.locator: §9, the final paragraph of the proof of Theorem 9.6, p. 311
items.note: Routed to the weight-monodromy Part II. Weight-monodromy passes to G-stable direct summands because N and the monodromy filtration are functorial (LPV.1).

items.name: Poincaré duality and Chern classes in ℓ-adic cohomology
items.statement: For a smooth proper variety of dimension d over an algebraically closed field (ℓ invertible): the cup-product pairing H^i × H^{2d−i} → Q̄_ℓ(−d) is perfect and Galois-equivariant, and H^{2d} of a connected one is one-dimensional; first Chern classes of line bundles, with c_1(L)^d ≠ 0 in H^{2d} for L ample.
items.locator: §9, proofs of Lemma 9.9 and Theorem 9.6, pp. 310–311
items.note: EDC.2:pairings plans the Frobenius/Galois-equivariant perfect pairing; EDC.3 plans Chern classes and the cycle class map compatible with intersections; degrees and positivity are SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.5.

items.name: Weight–monodromy purity of a Weil–Deligne or local Galois representation
items.statement: Let k be a local field with residue field 𝔽_q of characteristic p, ℓ ≠ p, and i ∈ ℤ. A Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representation (r, N) of W_k on a finite-dimensional Q̄_ℓ-vector space V satisfies weight–monodromy of weight i (is pure of weight i in the sense of Taylor–Yoshida) if, for the monodromy filtration Fil^N_• of the nilpotent N (the unique increasing filtration with N Fil^N_j ⊂ Fil^N_{j−2} and N^j : gr^N_j V ≅ gr^N_{−j} V for j ≥ 0), for every j ∈ ℤ and every geometric Frobenius Φ ∈ W_k, every eigenvalue of r(Φ) on gr^N_j V is a Weil q-number of weight i + j. A continuous representation of G_k on V satisfies weight–monodromy of weight i if the Frobenius semisimplification of its Weil–Deligne representation (Grothendieck's ℓ-adic monodromy theorem) does.
items.locator: §9, Conjecture 9.3, p. 308 (the property of V = H^i(X_k̄, Q̄_ℓ) asserted there); §1, Conjecture 1.14, p. 250
items.note: Split from item 140 by RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12/7. No stage text or packet node defines it, and several layers use it: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems:R24.5/compatible-system-predicates ('strictly pure'), AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.3/strict-compatibility-and-the-monodromy-weight-purity, AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII:AG2.5 and AG2.6/polarized-compatible-system-strictly-pure, and WeightsInEtaleCohomology:R34.6, which asks for the exact local monodromy-weight theorem. Routed by route 7 to DeligneWeightsAndPurity:DWP.5, which imports LPV.1's N and monodromy filtration and owns the weights of the monodromy graded pieces; the Weil–Deligne representation comes from ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2 and Weil numbers from DWP.0. LPV.1 is not the owner: it proves the filtration 'independently of any claim that these pieces have the corresponding Frobenius weights'. R19.3, R24.5, AG2.5, AG2.6 and R34.6 should import it from DWP.5, and so should the weight–monodromy Part II of route 6.

routes.reason: Sch12 is already the primary source of PerfectoidSpaces, and the roadmap's blueprint packet (research/blueprint/packets/PerfectoidSpaces--P0.json, 324 nodes over P0–P7, which replaced the 33-node decomposition data/decompositions/PerfectoidSpaces.json) plans every item of §§3–7. It also plans the three statements this route names, so the route adds Sch12 as a source for planned items rather than new mathematics. P1: Remark 5.14, that W(R) is the unique flat p-adically complete deformation of a perfect 𝔽_p-algebra (item 71), is an acceptance criterion of P1/cotangent-complex-vanishing-mod-varpi. P3: the invariance of absolute Galois groups under completion of a henselian field and under purely inseparable extension (item 2) is part of P3/fontaine-wintenberger; the atlas finding PerfectoidSpaces/E23 that called its omission from §1 a gap was rejected by REV-PerfectoidSpaces--P0. Remark 1.11, the recovery of Faltings's almost purity theorem for the tower R_n = K°⟨T^{±1/p^n}⟩ from Theorem 7.9, with S° = Ŝ_∞ and descent to the uncompleted tower (item 5), is an acceptance criterion of P3/almost-purity-theorem, which the paper only sketches.

§2 recalls Huber's theory. Most of it is in Tau Ceti (Huber rings, Spa, rational subsets, spectrality, units and plus ring detected on Spa) or planned by the Tau Ceti roadmap Foundations of adic spaces (rational localisation, 𝒪_X, sheafiness, adic spaces); the Berkovich comparison is TropicalAndBerkovichArithmetic TB.0 and ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H3. One recalled result has no owner: the universal property of maps into an affinoid adic space, Hom(Y, Spa(R,R⁺)) = Hom((R̂,R̂⁺), (𝒪_Y(Y),𝒪_Y⁺(Y))) (item 23). Foundations of adic spaces Layer 5 defines affinoid adic spaces without it, and AdicSpacesPartII:R0 (morphisms and fibre products) is where it belongs. The route also names two planned items for which Sch12 is a source: Huber's comparison of rigid-analytic varieties with adic spaces (item 25), planned in R1 by the packet nodes R1/rigid-adic-comparison-functor, R1/rigid-adic-quasi-separated-equivalence and R1/rigid-adic-topos-equivalence; and the specialisation map with X ≅ lim_𝔛 𝔛 over formal models (item 26), planned in R2 by R2/specialisation-map (v) and R2/raynaud-theorem (e).

TB.0 plans Berkovich spectra and their comparison with Huber's adic spectra through rank-one points and maximal generalisations, for strictly affinoid algebras; that covers the injection onto rank-one points and the maximal-Hausdorff retraction of Theorem 2.24 (planned item item 28). Sch12 also recalls the global statement (Huber [22, 8.3.1, 8.1.8]): tautness (quasiseparated, closures of quasicompact opens quasicompact) and the equivalence between Hausdorff strictly k-analytic Berkovich spaces and taut adic spaces locally of finite type (item 27). That is TB.0's gluing of affinoids into analytic spaces carried to the adic side, so it belongs in TB.0.

Proposition 2.27 (points of Spa(R, R⁺) ↔ maps to complete affinoid fields with dense image, item 31) and Proposition 2.29 (specialisation x ≻ y iff K ≅ L and L⁺ ⊂ K⁺; the generalisations of a point form a chain of length its rank, item 33) are point-set facts about Spa (Huber 1996, (1.1.6)–(1.1.10)) and belong to AdicSpacesPartII:R0. R0/adic-valuation-rings-and-centres, R0/fibre-over-point and R0/maximal-point-closure-rational cite Huber (1.1.8)–(1.1.10) in their proof steps, but no node states them; R0/fibre-over-point also uses the completed residue affinoid field κ(y), requested from the AdicSpaces anchor's Layer 5. This route was a source route to AdicEtaleGeometry:A1, whose stage concerns étale and finite étale sites; RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12/4 (confirmed) corrects the owner of the same two items. The AdicSpacesPartII blueprint was finished and promoted on 28 September 2026, before this extraction, and a source route does not re-run a finished blueprint. This route therefore records the owner only: items 31 and 33 become planned only after a packet amendment adds R0 nodes for them (RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12.fixes.md, 'For the maintainer').

routes.title: Analytic toric geometry, Part II: nonarchimedean models and perfectoid approximation
routes.brief: The parent already has a Part II: the accepted restructuring RS-32 makes Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactifications) 'Analytic toric geometry, Part II: arithmetic toroidal compactifications'. Build beside it, with Analytic toric geometry as first prerequisite: import ShimuraCompactifications:C0's toric charts over base rings and plan only what C0 lacks, namely fan gluing over a nonarchimedean field and its valuation ring, formal completion, and adic and perfectoid toric spaces. The queue designs this route as AnalyticToricGeometryPartII (job DESIGN-AnalyticToricGeometryPartII); whether it is numbered Part II or Part III beside ShimuraCompactifications is the maintainer's choice. PAPER-BINDA-KATO-VEZZANI-25 proposed a toric Part II with this title (its route 14). That extraction is under revision (review verdict 'revise') and none of its routes is queued; when it is resubmitted, its toric route should import this roadmap rather than propose its own. Its review held that route because the brief gave endpoints without the generic-base divisor, formal-model and approximation construction leaves (gap G12, research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BINDA-KATO-VEZZANI-25.review.json, route 14; the route itself is in research/blueprint/papers/PAPER-BINDA-KATO-VEZZANI-25.result.json). Scholze's §8 is the source of those leaves, and this brief states them below. Final theorems, as stated in Perfectoid spaces §8: Theorem 8.5 — for a fan Σ and a perfectoid field K with tilt K♭, (i) X^perf_{Σ,K} tilts to X^perf_{Σ,K♭}; (ii) X^perf_{Σ,K} ∼ lim_φ X^ad_{Σ,K}; (iii) |X^ad_{Σ,K♭}| ≅ lim_φ |X^ad_{Σ,K}|, defining π; (iv) (X^ad_{Σ,K♭})~_ét ≅ lim_φ (X^ad_{Σ,K})~_ét; (v) compatibility with every open U and its preimage. Proposition 8.6 — for X_Σ proper smooth, ℓ ≠ p and K algebraically closed, π gives H^i(X^ad_{Σ,K,ét}, ℤ/ℓ^m) ≅ H^i(X^ad_{Σ,K♭,ét}, ℤ/ℓ^m). Proposition 8.7 — for X_{Σ,K} proper smooth, a hypersurface Y and a small open neighbourhood Ỹ of Y^ad, there is a hypersurface Z ⊂ X_{Σ,K♭} with Z^ad ⊂ π^{-1}(Ỹ), defined over any given dense subfield of K♭. Corollary 8.8 — for X_{Σ,K} projective smooth and Y a set-theoretic complete intersection of codimension c, there is a closed Z ⊂ X_{Σ,K♭} with Z^ad ⊂ π^{-1}(Ỹ) and dim Z = dim Y, over a given dense subfield. Also Theorem 1.5 for the affine line, by restricting (iii) for the complete fan of ℙ¹ to 𝔸¹ = ℙ¹ ∖ {∞}, which φ preserves. Leaves to construct, in order. (1) Generic-base toric schemes: for any ring A, U_σ = Spec A[σ^∨ ∩ M] and the open immersions for faces, imported from Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry C0 (ShimuraCompactifications:C0, which extends affine toric charts from ℂ to the base rings of integral models; packet nodes C0/relative-torus-embedding and C0/relative-face-open with the trivial torsor) and not rebuilt, with the dual semigroup σ^∨ ∩ M and its finite generation (Gordan) taken from Analytic toric geometry Layer 0 item 6. If the owner question of RT-AREA-algebraicgeometry/34 gives the glued general-base X(Σ) to C0, import that too; otherwise glue here along the fan axioms: X_{Σ,A} with torus, action and base point, base change in A. For A = ℂ, prove that X_{Σ,ℂ}, with its torus, torus action and affine charts, agrees with the fan scheme of Analytic toric geometry Layer 0 item 9 (PROTOCOL §15: a general construction is compatible with the special case it subsumes); Definition 8.1 and the classification Theorem 8.3 over a field (with Sumihiro), or state the fan form X_Σ as the input of Theorem 9.6. (2) Invariant divisors: primitive ray generators v_i (Tau Ceti has them), D_i, T-Weil divisors ⊕ℤD_i, every Weil divisor equivalent to one, and H⁰(X_{Σ,A}, 𝒪(D)) = ⊕_{⟨u,v_i⟩ ≥ −a_i} Aχ^u over any A, with the integral model over K° and local trivialisations of 𝒪(D) by characters, so |f(x)| is defined up to a unit of K° (the 'tautological integral model' of Proposition 8.7). (3) The adic toric space X^ad_Σ = generic fibre of the formal completion of X_{Σ,K°} (glued from Spa(K⟨σ^∨∩M⟩, K°⟨σ^∨∩M⟩)), equal to (X_Σ)^ad when Σ is complete; φ from multiplication by p on M. (4) The perfectoid toric space from K⟨(σ^∨∩M)[p^{-1}]⟩, perfectoid by the argument of Proposition 5.20, with sheaves 𝒪(D) for D ∈ ⊕ℤ[p^{-1}]D_i and H⁰ the completed span of the χ^u. (5) The graded ring R_D = completion of ⊕_{j∈ℤ[p^{-1}]} H⁰(X^perf, 𝒪(jD)) for D = Σ_i a_i D_i: identify R_D with the Banach-completed perfected monoid algebra K⟨C_D ∩ (M[p^{-1}] × ℤ[p^{-1}])⟩ of the rational polyhedral cone C_D = {(u, j) ∈ M_ℝ × ℝ : ⟨u, v_i⟩ ≥ −j a_i for all i}, graded by (u, j) ↦ j, so that R_D is perfectoid and its tilt is the same construction over K♭. Do not reprove the approximation induction of Lemma 6.5. routes.title: Deligne weights, purity and the Weil bounds, Part II: the ℓ-adic weight–monodromy conjecture for toric complete intersections
routes.brief: The parent already has a Part II: the accepted restructuring RS-17 makes Weights and purity in étale cohomology (WeightsInEtaleCohomology) 'Deligne weights, purity and the Weil bounds, Part II: Arithmetic cohomology and eigenform applications'. Build beside it, with DeligneWeightsAndPurity as first prerequisite and no dependence on WeightsInEtaleCohomology. Its R34.6 stops at stating the exact local monodromy-weight theorem its applications need, and assumes no general weight–monodromy; it may consume Theorem 9.6 from here. The queue designs this route as DeligneWeightsAndPurityPartII (job DESIGN-DeligneWeightsAndPurityPartII); whether it is numbered Part II or Part III beside WeightsInEtaleCohomology is the maintainer's choice. Extend Deligne weights, purity and the Weil bounds (DeligneWeightsAndPurity) from Deligne's equal-characteristic local weight theory (DWP.5) to mixed characteristic, following Scholze, Perfectoid spaces, §9. Final theorem, exactly as Theorem 9.6: let k be a local field of characteristic 0 and Y a geometrically connected proper smooth variety over k that is a set-theoretic complete intersection in a projective smooth toric variety X_Σ; then the weight-monodromy conjecture holds for Y. Import from DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.5 the predicate 'V satisfies weight–monodromy of weight i' for a finite-dimensional Q̄_ℓ-representation V of G_k (ℓ ≠ p), or a Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representation: for all j and every geometric Frobenius Φ, every eigenvalue of Φ on gr_j^N V is a Weil q-number of weight i + j (item 154 of this extraction, routed to DWP.5 by route 7; N and Fil^N from LPV.1, Weil numbers from DWP.0). State here Conjecture 9.3 for a proper smooth variety, 'WMC holds for X' (item 140), and prove the predicate's stability under finite extension of k, under restriction to G_K for K the completion of k(ϖ^{1/p^∞}) (totally ramified and pro-p: geometric Frobenii and pro-ℓ inertia survive), and under passage to G-stable direct summands. Construct the identification G_K ≅ G_{K♭} ≅ G_{k′}, k′ = 𝔽_q((t)), t = ϖ♭, from PerfectoidSpaces P3 (Theorem 1.3) and the invariance of Galois groups under completion and perfection (planned in P3 by PerfectoidSpaces:P3/fontaine-wintenberger), and prove it matches inertia, t_ℓ, Frobenius and N. Prove or import Huber's theorem [Hub98, Theorem 3.6(a)] that some open neighbourhood Ỹ of Y^ad in X^ad_{Σ,K} has the same ℤ/ℓ^m-cohomology over ℂ_p as Y^ad, and use Huber's comparison of algebraic and adic étale cohomology (ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H5, Theorem 9.7). From 'Analytic toric geometry, Part II: nonarchimedean models and perfectoid approximation' (route 5 of this extraction, designed as AnalyticToricGeometryPartII) import π, Proposition 8.6 and Corollary 8.8 (Z ⊂ X_{Σ,K♭} with Z^ad ⊂ π^{-1}(Ỹ), dim Z = dim Y, defined over a global function field, geometrically irreducible), and take a projective smooth alteration Z′ (AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5). Build the G-equivariant diagram of étale topoi and the map H^i(Y_{ℂ_p}) = H^i(Ỹ_{ℂ_p}) → H^i(Z′_{ℂ_p♭}), prove cup-product compatibility (Lemma 9.8: pullback along a morphism of sites respects cup products, as composition in the derived category), prove the top-degree isomorphism (Lemma 9.9) from Proposition 8.6 and the nonvanishing of c_1(L)^{dim Y} on Z′ for L ample (EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.3), deduce with Poincaré duality (EDC.2:pairings) that H^i(Y) is a G-stable direct summand of H^i(Z′), and conclude from Deligne's theorem for Z′ (DWP.5 with DWP.4/DWP.7 purity; Theorem 9.4 needs Z′ spread out over a curve over 𝔽_q). Imports: DeligneWeightsAndPurity DWP.0, DWP.4, DWP.5, DWP.7; LefschetzPencilsAndVanishingCycles LPV.1 (t_ℓ, N, monodromy filtration); ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations R01.2 (Frobenius–N relation convention); Local fields and ramification (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification) Layer 4; PerfectoidSpaces P3; the nonarchimedean toric roadmap of route 5 (AnalyticToricGeometryPartII); ClassicalAdicEtaleCohomology H5; AdicCoefficientsAndComparisons L5; EtaleDualityAndPerverseSheaves EDC.2, EDC.3; SchemeAndStackFoundations SF.2, SF.5. Do not assume the general mixed-characteristic conjecture (R34.6), and keep Rapoport–Zink's semistable surface case and the Shimura-variety cases out of scope. Tests: Y = ℙⁿ (trivially pure); a smooth hypersurface in ℙⁿ; a smooth plane curve (where the statement is Grothendieck's monodromy theorem plus the curve case); and the non-example of a variety that is not a set-theoretic complete intersection, for which the method gives no statement.
routes.reason: No stage owns the weight-monodromy conjecture in mixed characteristic: DWP.5 proves Deligne's local weight theorem for curves over finite fields and states that it is not the mixed-characteristic conjecture, and WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.6 forbids assuming it. Scholze's theorem is a direct extension of that weight theory, proved by reducing to DWP.5's equal-characteristic theorem through perfectoid tilting, so it is a Part II of Deligne weights, purity and the Weil bounds, not a new roadmap. The accepted RS-17 already makes WeightsInEtaleCohomology the Part II of this parent, but its R34.6 only states the local monodromy-weight input its applications need, so this route is a second continuation beside it, which R34.6 may consume (RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12/1). The p-adic analogue proposed by BKV (parent PadicDifferentialEquationsAndRigidCohomology) concerns Hyodo–Kato cohomology and is a different statement; that extraction is under revision and its route is not queued (RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12/2). The weight–monodromy predicate for a representation is planned at DWP.5 (route 7; RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12/7).

Weight–monodromy purity of a Weil–Deligne representation is a general notion that several layers use and none defines: PotentialModularityAndCompatibleSystems R24.5 ('strictly pure'), AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations R19.3, AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII AG2.5 and AG2.6, and WeightsInEtaleCohomology R34.6. PROTOCOL §15 plans it once, in its most foundational owner. DWP.5 imports LPV.1's nilpotent logarithm and monodromy filtration and proves 'the weights of the monodromy graded pieces', so it owns the predicate. LPV.1 does not: it proves the filtration 'independently of any claim that these pieces have the corresponding Frobenius weights', and says 'DWP.5 owns the later local weight estimates'. Sch12's Conjecture 9.3 is a source for the definition (item 154). The conjecture for varieties (item 140) and Scholze's theorem stay in route 6, which imports the predicate from DWP.5. This route was added by FIX-RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12 for RT-PAPER-SCHOLZE-12/7, whose verifier prescribed it. The extraction's review (PAPER-SCHOLZE-12.review.json) has no verdict for route 7, so the queue does not apply this route until the next review of the extraction accepts it.
